bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第186卷卷第一百八十六

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 186, the one hundred and eighty-sixth volume.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 186

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二】 起著雍攝提格八月，盡十二月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 2] — beginning in the eighth month of zhiyong shetige, through the twelfth month, less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records, Part 2] — from the eighth month of the year Wuyin (618 CE) through the twelfth month, less than a full year.

sentences.zh: 八月，薛舉遣其子仁果進圍寧州，刺史胡演擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Xue Ju sent his son Renguo to advance and besiege Ning Prefecture; the prefect Hu Yan repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Xue Ju sent his son Renguo to press the siege of Ning Prefecture, but Prefect Hu Yan drove him back.

sentences.zh: 郝瑗言於舉曰：「今唐兵新破，關中騷動，宜乘勝直取長安。」

translations.literal: Hao Yuan said to Ju, "The Tang forces have just been defeated and Guanzhong is in turmoil; we ought to seize the victory and strike straight for Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yuan urged Ju, "The Tang army has just been beaten and Guanzhong is in uproar — we should ride this victory straight to Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 舉然之，會有疾而止。

translations.literal: Ju agreed, but illness intervened and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ju agreed, but fell ill before he could act.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，舉卒。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Ju died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, Xue Ju died.

sentences.zh: 太子仁果立，居於折址城，謚舉曰武帝。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Renguo was enthroned, residing at Zhezhi City; Ju was given the posthumous title Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Renguo succeeded him and made his seat at Zhezhi City; Ju was posthumously titled Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 上欲與李軌共圖秦、隴，遣使潛詣涼州，招撫之，與之書，謂之從弟。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to join Li Gui in a common plan against Qin and Long, and sent envoys secretly to Liang Prefecture to win him over; he wrote him a letter and called him his younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hoped to ally with Li Gui against Qin and Long, and sent secret envoys to Liang Prefecture to win him over, addressing him in a letter as his younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 軌大喜，遣其弟懋入貢。

translations.literal: Li Gui was greatly pleased and sent his younger brother Mao to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui was delighted and sent his brother Mao to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 上以懋為大將軍，命鴻臚少卿張俟德冊拜軌為涼州總管，封涼王。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Mao Grand General and ordered the Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Zhang Houde to invest Li Gui as Overall Commander of Liang Prefecture and enfeoff him as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Mao a grand general and charged Vice Director Zhang Houde of the Court of Imperial Entertainments to invest Li Gui as overall commander of Liang Prefecture and enfeoff him as Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷以安陽令呂鈱為相州刺史，更以相州刺史王德仁為巖州刺史。

translations.literal: Initially the court had appointed Lü Yin, magistrate of Anyang, as prefect of Xiang Prefecture, and transferred the former prefect Wang Deren to be prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had named Lü Yin, magistrate of Anyang, prefect of Xiang, and moved the sitting prefect Wang Deren to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德仁由是怨憤，甲申，誘山東大使宇文明達入林慮山而殺之，叛歸王世充。

translations.literal: Deren therefore bore resentment; on the day jiashen he lured the ambassador for Shandong Yu Wenhua Mingda into the Linlu Mountains and killed him, then defected to Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Deren nursed a grudge over this; on the day jiashen he lured the Shandong envoy Yu Wenhua Mingda into the Linlu Mountains and killed him, then went over to Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 已丑，以秦王世民為元帥，擊薛仁果。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, the Prince of Qin Shimin was appointed supreme commander to attack Xue Renguo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Prince of Qin Li Shimin was made supreme commander to strike Xue Renguo.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，臨洮等四郡來降。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, four prefectures including Lintao submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, four prefectures including Lintao came over.

sentences.zh: 隋江都太守陳稜求得煬帝之柩，取宇文化及所留輦輅鼓吹，粗備天子儀衛，改葬於江都宮西吳公台下，其王公以下，皆列瘞於帝塋之側。

translations.literal: Chen Leng, grand governor of Jiangdu under Sui, obtained Emperor Yang's coffin, took the imperial carriages, regalia, and musical instruments Yu Wenhuaji had left behind, and roughly equipped a full imperial escort; he reburied him west of the palace at Jiangdu, below the Wu Duke's Terrace, and buried the princes and officials in rows beside the imperial tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Leng, Sui's grand governor of Jiangdu, recovered Emperor Yang's coffin, took the carriages, regalia, and musicians Yu Wenhuaji had abandoned, and mustered a rough version of the imperial funeral train; he reinterred the emperor west of the Jiangdu palace, below the Wu Duke's Terrace, with princes and officials buried in rows beside the mound.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之發江都也，以杜伏威為歷陽太守；

translations.literal: When Yu Wenhuaji departed Jiangdu, he had appointed Du Fuwei grand governor of Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Wenhuaji marched out of Jiangdu, he had named Du Fuwei governor of Liyang;

sentences.zh: 伏威不受，仍上表於隋，皇泰主拜伏威為東道大總管，封楚王。

translations.literal: Fuwei did not accept it but still submitted a memorial to Sui; Emperor Huangtai appointed Fuwei Grand Commander of the Eastern Circuit and enfeoffed him as Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei refused the post and instead memorialized the Sui court; Emperor Huangtai made him grand commander of the eastern circuit and enfeoffed him as Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 沈法興亦上表於皇泰主。

translations.literal: Shen Faxing also submitted a memorial to Emperor Huangtai.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Faxing likewise sent a memorial to Emperor Huangtai.

sentences.zh: 自稱大司馬、錄尚書事、天門公，承製置百官，以陳杲仁為司徒，孫士漢為司空，蔣元超為左僕射，殷芊為左丞，徐令言為右丞，劉子翼為選部侍郎，李百藥為府椽。

translations.literal: He styled himself Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of Heavenly Gate; acting on imperial edict he installed the full bureaucracy, appointing Chen Gaoren Minister over the Masses, Sun Shihan Minister of Works, Jiang Yuanchao Left Vice Director, Yin Qian Left Assistant, Xu Lingyan Right Assistant, Liu Ziyi Vice Director of the Selection Bureau, and Li Baiyao a staff clerk in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He took the titles Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of Heavenly Gate, and by imperial commission set up a full bureaucracy: Chen Gaoren as Minister over the Masses, Sun Shihan as Minister of Works, Jiang Yuanchao as left vice director, Yin Qian as left assistant, Xu Lingyan as right assistant, Liu Ziyi as vice director of the selection bureau, and Li Baiyao as a headquarters clerk.

sentences.zh: 百藥，德林之子也。

translations.literal: Baiyao was the son of Delin.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was the son of Li Delin.

sentences.zh: 九月，隋襄國通守陳君賓來降，拜邢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Chen Junbin, communications-and-defense commissioner of Xiangguo under Sui, came to submit and was appointed prefect of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Chen Junbin, Sui's commissioner at Xiangguo, defected and was made prefect of Xing.

sentences.zh: 君賓，伯山之子也。

translations.literal: Junbin was the son of Boshan.
translations.idiomatic: Junbin was the son of Chen Boshan.

sentences.zh: 虞州刺史韋義節攻隋河東通守堯君素，久不下，軍數不利；

translations.literal: Wei Yijie, prefect of Yu Prefecture, attacked Yao Junsu, communications-and-defense commissioner of Hedong under Sui, but could not take him for a long time and suffered repeated setbacks in battle;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yijie, prefect of Yu, besieged Yao Junsu, Sui's commissioner in Hedong, but failed to reduce the city after a long campaign and lost battle after battle;

sentences.zh: 壬子，以工部尚書獨孤懷恩代之。

translations.literal: on the day renzi he was replaced by Dugu Huai'en, Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: on the day renzi, Dugu Huai'en, Minister of Public Works, was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 初，李密既殺翟讓，頗自驕矜，不恤士眾；

translations.literal: Initially, after Li Mi had killed Zhai Rang, he grew quite arrogant and proud and did not care for his soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi killed Zhai Rang, he grew arrogant and stopped looking after his men;

sentences.zh: 倉粟雖多，無府庫錢帛，戰士有功，無以為賞；

translations.literal: though the granaries held much grain, there was no money or silk in the treasury, and warriors who earned merit had nothing with which to be rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: the granaries were full but the treasury held no cash or silk, so there was nothing with which to reward men who fought well;

sentences.zh: 又厚撫初附之人，眾心頗怨。

translations.literal: he also lavished favors on those who had just joined him, and hearts among the ranks grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: meanwhile he showered favors on new recruits, and morale in the ranks turned sour.

sentences.zh: 徐世勣嘗因宴會刺譏其短；

translations.literal: Xu Shiji once used a banquet to needle him about his faults;
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Xu Shiji once needled him about these failings;

sentences.zh: 密不懌，使世勣出鎮黎陽，雖名委任，實亦疏之。

translations.literal: Mi was displeased and sent Shiji out to garrison Liyang; though this bore the name of a major commission, in truth he was being pushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: Mi took offense and posted Shiji to garrison Liyang — a grand title in name, but in truth a way to keep him at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 密開洛口倉散米，無防守典當者，又無文券，取之者隨意多少；

translations.literal: Mi opened the Luokou granary and gave out grain; there were no guards or clerks in charge, and no ration tickets — those who took grain could take as much or as little as they wished;
translations.idiomatic: Mi opened the Luokou granary and handed out grain with no guards, no clerks, and no ration slips — people took whatever they pleased;

sentences.zh: 或離倉之後，力不能致，委棄衢路，自倉城至郭門，米厚數寸，為車馬所躪踐；

translations.literal: some, after leaving the granary, lacked the strength to carry what they had taken and abandoned it in the streets; from the granary wall to the city gate the grain lay inches deep, trampled by carts and horses;
translations.idiomatic: many could not carry what they had taken and dumped it in the roads; from the granary to the city gate grain lay inches deep, ground under wheels and hooves;

sentences.zh: 群盜來就食者並家屬近百萬口，無甕盎，織荊筐淘米，洛水兩岸十里之間，望之皆如白沙。

translations.literal: bandits who came for food, with their families, numbered nearly a million mouths; having no jars or bowls, they wove thorn baskets to wash grain; for ten li along both banks of the Luo River the scene looked like white sand.
translations.idiomatic: nearly a million mouths — bandits and families alike — came to eat; without pots or bowls they wove thorn baskets to wash grain, and for ten li along both banks of the Luo the scene looked like a beach of white sand.

sentences.zh: 密喜，謂賈閏甫曰：「此可謂足食矣！」

translations.literal: Mi was pleased and said to Jia Runfu, "This may be called having food in abundance!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi was delighted and told Jia Runfu, "Surely we have food enough now!"

sentences.zh: 閏甫對曰：「國以民為本，民以食為天。

translations.literal: Runfu replied, "A state takes the people as its foundation, and the people take food as their heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Runfu answered, "A state rests on its people, and the people rest on their food.

sentences.zh: 今民所以襁負如流而至者，以所天在此故也。

translations.literal: The reason the people now come in swaddled bundles, flowing like a stream, is that their heaven is here.
translations.idiomatic: They flock here carrying their children because their heaven — their food — is here.

sentences.zh: 而有司曾無愛吝，屑越如此！

translations.literal: Yet the officials show not the slightest care or thrift and waste it like this!
translations.idiomatic: Yet your officials show no care at all and squander it like refuse!

sentences.zh: 竊恐一旦米盡民散，明公孰與成大業哉！」

translations.literal: I fear that once the grain is gone the people will scatter — with whom then, my lord, will you accomplish the great enterprise?"
translations.idiomatic: I fear that when the grain runs out the people will scatter — and then with whom will you build your great enterprise?"

sentences.zh: 密謝之，即以閏甫判司倉參軍事。

translations.literal: Mi thanked him and at once appointed Runfu acting staff officer of the Granary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Mi thanked him and immediately made Runfu acting staff officer of the granary bureau.

sentences.zh: 密以東都兵數敗微弱，而將相自相屠滅，謂朝夕可平。

translations.literal: Mi believed the Eastern Capital's forces had been repeatedly defeated and were weak, and that its generals and ministers were slaughtering one another; he thought it could be pacified within days.
translations.idiomatic: Mi thought the Eastern Capital army had been beaten down to weakness and that its commanders were killing one another — he expected to take the city within days.

sentences.zh: 王世充既專大權，厚賞將士，繕治器械，亦陰圖取密。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, having seized full power, richly rewarded his officers and soldiers and repaired weapons and equipment; he also secretly plotted to take Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, now holding sole power, lavished rewards on his troops and refurbished arms and gear while secretly plotting to destroy Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 時隋軍乏食，而密軍少衣，世充請交易，密難之；

translations.literal: At that time the Sui army lacked food while Mi's army lacked clothing; Shichong proposed an exchange, and Mi found it difficult to accept;
translations.idiomatic: The Sui side was short of food and Mi's army short of clothing; Shichong proposed a swap, which Mi was reluctant to grant;

sentences.zh: 長史邴元真等各求私利，勸密許之。

translations.literal: the Chief Administrator Bing Yuanzhen and others each sought private gain and urged Mi to agree.
translations.idiomatic: but Chief Administrator Bing Yuanzhen and others, each chasing private profit, urged Mi to agree.

sentences.zh: 先是，東都人歸密者，日以百數；

translations.literal: Previously, people from the Eastern Capital who defected to Mi numbered in the hundreds each day;
translations.idiomatic: Until then hundreds from the Eastern Capital had been defecting to Mi every day;

sentences.zh: 既得食，降者益少，密悔而止。

translations.literal: once they had obtained food, defectors grew fewer by the day, and Mi regretted it and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: once they had been fed, fewer came over each day, and Mi regretted the trade and called it off.

sentences.zh: 密破宇文化及還，其勁卒良馬多死，士卒疲病。

translations.literal: After Mi defeated Yu Wenhuaji and returned, many of his crack troops and fine horses had died and his soldiers were weary and ill.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi returned from defeating Yu Wenhuaji, his best troops and horses were largely dead and his men were exhausted and sick.

sentences.zh: 世充欲乘其弊擊之，恐人心不壹，乃詐稱左軍衛士張永通三夢周公，令宣意於世充，當勒兵相助擊賊。

translations.literal: Shichong wished to strike while Mi was weakened but feared hearts were not united; he therefore falsely claimed that Zhang Yongtong, a guardsman of the Left Army, had thrice dreamed of the Duke of Zhou, who ordered him to tell Shichong that he must marshal troops to help attack the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong wanted to strike while Mi was weak but feared his men were not of one mind; he therefore fabricated a story that Zhang Yongtong, a guardsman of the Left Army, had thrice dreamed that the Duke of Zhou told him Shichong must raise troops to help crush the rebel.

sentences.zh: 乃為周公立廟，每出兵，輒先祈禱。

translations.literal: He therefore built a temple to the Duke of Zhou, and whenever he took the field he would first pray there.
translations.idiomatic: He built a temple to the Duke of Zhou and prayed there before every campaign.

sentences.zh: 世充令巫宣言周公欲令僕射急討李密，當有大功，不即兵皆疫死。

translations.literal: Shichong had shamans proclaim that the Duke of Zhou wished the Director to hurry and attack Li Mi, that great merit awaited, and that if he did not act at once all the troops would die of plague.
translations.idiomatic: His shamans proclaimed that the Duke of Zhou wanted the Director to attack Li Mi at once for great merit — otherwise every soldier would die of plague.

sentences.zh: 世充兵多楚人，信妖言，皆請戰。

translations.literal: Many of Shichong's troops were men of Chu and believed these portents; all clamored for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Shichong's men were Chu natives who believed such omens, and all clamored to fight.

sentences.zh: 世充簡練精銳得二萬餘人，馬二千餘匹，壬子，出師擊密，旗幡之上皆書永通字，軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: Shichong selected and drilled crack troops numbering more than twenty thousand, with more than two thousand horses; on the day renzi he marched out to attack Mi, writing the character Yongtong on every banner — his army's appearance was most imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong mustered more than twenty thousand picked troops and over two thousand horses; on the day renzi he marched against Mi with Yongtong's name on every banner — a formidable host.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，至偃師，營於通濟渠南，作三橋於渠上。

translations.literal: On the day guichou he reached Yanshi and encamped south of the Tongji Canal, building three bridges across the channel.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou he reached Yanshi, camped south of the Tongji Canal, and threw three bridges across it.

sentences.zh: 密留王伯當守金墉，自引精兵出偃師北，阻邙山以待之。

translations.literal: Mi left Wang Bodang to hold Jinyong and himself led crack troops north of Yanshi, taking position on Mount Mang to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi left Wang Bodang to hold Jinyong and led his elite north of Yanshi, blocking Mount Mang to await him.

sentences.zh: 密召諸將會議，裴仁基曰：「世充悉眾而至，洛下必虛，可分兵守其要路，令不得東，簡精兵三萬，傍河西出以逼東都。

translations.literal: Mi summoned his generals to council; Pei Renji said, "Shichong has brought his entire force; the Eastern Capital must be empty. We can divide troops to hold the key roads and keep him from returning east, select thirty thousand crack troops, and march west along the river to press the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mi called his generals to council. Pei Renji said, "Shichong has marched out with everything he has — Luoyang must be hollow. Detach men to hold the key roads so he cannot return east, pick thirty thousand elite troops, and march west along the river to threaten the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世充還，我且按甲；

translations.literal: When Shichong returns, we hold our arms;
translations.idiomatic: When he turns back, we hold our ground;

sentences.zh: 世充再出，我又逼之。

translations.literal: when he comes out again, we press him once more.
translations.idiomatic: when he marches out again, we threaten him again.

sentences.zh: 如此，則我有餘力，彼勞奔命，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: In this way we keep our strength in reserve while he wears himself out running to and fro — his defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: That way we fight fresh while he exhausts himself — and he is sure to fall."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「公言大善。

translations.literal: Mi said, "Your words are excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "Excellent advice.

sentences.zh: 今東都兵有三不可當：兵仗精銳，一也；

translations.literal: But the Eastern Capital's army has three things that make it hard to face: their arms are keen and sharp — that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Eastern Capital army has three reasons we should not meet them head-on: their weapons are sharp — first;

sentences.zh: 決計深入，二也；

translations.literal: they are resolved to drive deep — that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: they are committed to a deep strike — second;

sentences.zh: 食盡求戰，三也。

translations.literal: their food is gone and they seek battle — that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: their food is gone and they are desperate to fight — third.

sentences.zh: 我但乘城固守，蓄力以待之；

translations.literal: We need only hold the walls and stand firm, storing our strength to await them;
translations.idiomatic: We need only hold our walls, husband our strength, and wait;

sentences.zh: 彼欲斗不得，求走無路，不過十日，世充之頭可致麾下。」

translations.literal: they will want to fight but cannot, and when they seek to flee will find no road — within ten days Shichong's head can be delivered to your command."
translations.idiomatic: they will want battle and find none; they will want escape and find no road — within ten days Shichong's head will be at your feet."

sentences.zh: 陳智略、樊文超、單雄信皆曰：「計世充戰卒甚少，屢經摧破，悉已喪膽。

translations.literal: Chen Zhilue, Fan Wenchao, and Shan Xiongxin all said, "We reckon Shichong's battle troops are very few and have been repeatedly shattered — they have all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilue, Fan Wenchao, and Shan Xiongxin all said, "Shichong's fighting men are few and have been beaten again and again — they are terrified.

sentences.zh: 《兵法》曰『倍則戰』，況不啻倍哉！

translations.literal: The Art of War says, 'When you have double the enemy's strength, fight' — how much more when we are far more than double!
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says that when you outnumber the enemy two to one, you fight — and we are far more than double!

sentences.zh: 且江、淮新附之士，望因此機展其勳效；

translations.literal: Moreover, the men newly attached from the Jiang and Huai regions hope by this chance to display their merit;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the men newly come from the Jiang and Huai hope to win glory in this fight;

sentences.zh: 及其鋒而用之，可以得志。」

translations.literal: strike while their edge is keen and we can achieve our aim."
translations.idiomatic: strike while their spirit is high and we will prevail."

sentences.zh: 於是諸將喧然，欲戰者什七八，密惑於眾議而從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals clamored; seven or eight in ten wanted battle, and Mi, swayed by the crowd, agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The generals clamored; seven or eight in ten wanted to fight, and Mi, swayed by the crowd, agreed.

sentences.zh: 仁基苦爭不得，擊地歎曰：「公後必悔之！」

translations.literal: Renji argued bitterly but could not prevail; he struck the ground and sighed, "My lord, you will surely regret this!"
translations.idiomatic: Renji argued in vain, struck the ground, and cried, "You will regret this!"

sentences.zh: 魏徵言於長史鄭頲曰：「魏公雖驟勝，而驍將銳卒多死，戰士心怠，此二者難以應敵。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said to Chief Administrator Zheng Ting, "Though the Duke of Wei has won sudden victories, many of his fierce generals and crack troops are dead and the soldiers' hearts are weary — these two things make it hard to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng told Chief Administrator Zheng Ting, "The Duke of Wei has won quick victories, but his best generals and troops are dead and his men are weary — with those two handicaps he cannot face the enemy.

sentences.zh: 且世充乏食，志在死戰，難與爭鋒，未若深溝高壘以拒之，不過旬月，世充糧盡，必自退，追而擊之，蔑不勝矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover Shichong lacks food and is resolved to fight to the death — it is hard to contend with his edge. Better to dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts to hold him off; within ten days or a month Shichong's grain will be gone and he will surely withdraw of himself; pursue and strike, and victory is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong is out of food and desperate — you cannot match his fury. Dig deep trenches and raise high walls instead; within a month his grain will run out and he will retreat; then pursue and you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 頲曰：「此老生之常談耳。」

translations.literal: Ting said, "That is the old pedant's usual talk."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said, "That is the old pedant's stock advice."

sentences.zh: 征曰：「此乃奇策，何謂常談！」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "This is a brilliant stratagem — how can you call it usual talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "This is a brilliant plan — how is that usual talk!"

sentences.zh: 拂衣而起。

translations.literal: He brushed his robe and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed off his robe and left.

sentences.zh: 程知節將內馬軍與密同營在北邙山上，單雄信將外馬軍營於偃師城北。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhijie commanded the inner horse army and encamped with Mi on Mount Mang north of Luoyang; Shan Xiongxin commanded the outer horse army and encamped north of Yanshi city.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhijie led the inner cavalry and camped with Mi on Mount Mang; Shan Xiongxin led the outer cavalry and camped north of Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 世充遣數百騎渡通濟渠攻雄信營，密遣裴行儼與知節助之。

translations.literal: Shichong sent several hundred horsemen across the Tongji Canal to attack Xiongxin's camp; Mi sent Pei Xingyan and Zhijie to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent several hundred horsemen across the Tongji Canal against Xiongxin's camp; Mi sent Pei Xingyan and Cheng Zhijie to help.

sentences.zh: 行儼先馳赴敵，中流矢，附於地；

translations.literal: Xingyan galloped ahead to meet the enemy, was struck by an arrow, and clung to the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Xingyan charged ahead and took an arrow; he slumped to the ground;

sentences.zh: 知節救之，殺數人，世充軍披靡，乃抱行儼重騎而還；

translations.literal: Zhijie rescued him, killed several men, and Shichong's army broke; he then lifted Xingyan onto his horse and rode back;
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie fought his way to him, killed several men, and routed Shichong's line; he hoisted Xingyan onto his horse and rode back;

sentences.zh: 為世充騎所逐，刺槊洞過，知節回身捩折其槊，兼斬追者，與行儼俱免。

translations.literal: Shichong's horsemen pursued him and thrust a lance clean through him; Zhijie turned, wrenched the lance and broke it, and also cut down his pursuers — he and Xingyan both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's riders pursued and drove a lance through him; Zhijie wheeled, snapped the lance, cut down his pursuers, and both men escaped.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，各斂兵還營。

translations.literal: At dusk both sides drew off their troops and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk both sides withdrew to camp.

sentences.zh: 密驍將孫長樂等十餘人皆被重創。

translations.literal: More than ten of Mi's fierce generals, including Sun Changle, were all badly wounded.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of Mi's best generals, including Sun Changle, were gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 密新破宇文化及，有輕世充之心，不設壁壘。

translations.literal: Mi, having just defeated Yu Wenhuaji, looked down on Shichong and did not build fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from defeating Yu Wenhuaji, Mi underestimated Shichong and built no fortifications.

sentences.zh: 世充夜遣二百餘騎潛入北山，伏溪谷中，命軍士皆秣馬蓐食。

translations.literal: Shichong by night sent more than two hundred horsemen secretly into the northern hills to lie in ambush in the ravines, ordering the soldiers to feed their horses and take their rations in the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: By night Shichong sent more than two hundred horsemen to hide in the northern hills and ravines, ordering every man to feed his horse and eat in the saddle.

sentences.zh: 甲寅旦，將戰，世充誓眾曰：「今日之戰，非直爭勝負；

translations.literal: At dawn on the day jiayin, as battle was about to begin, Shichong swore his troops: "Today's fight is not merely over victory or defeat;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the day jiayin, before battle, Shichong addressed his men: "Today's fight is not merely about winning or losing;

sentences.zh: 死生之分，在此一舉。

translations.literal: the line between life and death hangs on this one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: life and death hang on this one stroke.

sentences.zh: 若其捷也，富貴固所不論；

translations.literal: If we win, wealth and rank need not be mentioned;
translations.idiomatic: If we win, wealth and rank go without saying;

sentences.zh: 若其不捷，必無一人獲免。

translations.literal: if we do not win, not one man will be spared.
translations.idiomatic: if we lose, not one of us will be spared.

sentences.zh: 所爭者死，非獨為國，各宜勉之！」

translations.literal: What we contend for is survival — not for the state alone. Each of you must exert himself!"
translations.idiomatic: We fight for our lives — not for the state alone. Every man must give his all!"

sentences.zh: 遲明，引兵薄密。

translations.literal: At first light he led his troops to press close on Mi.
translations.idiomatic: At first light he advanced on Mi.

sentences.zh: 密出兵應之，未及成列，世充縱兵擊之。

translations.literal: Mi sent troops out to meet him, but before they could form ranks Shichong loosed his army upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Mi marched out to meet him, but before his men could form ranks Shichong charged.

sentences.zh: 世充士卒皆江、淮剽勇，出入如飛。

translations.literal: Shichong's soldiers were all fierce fighters from the Jiang and Huai, darting in and out like flight.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's men were Jiang and Huai veterans who struck like lightning.

sentences.zh: 世充先索得一人貌類密者，縛而匿之。

translations.literal: Shichong had earlier found a man who resembled Mi in appearance, bound him, and kept him hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had already found a man who looked like Li Mi, bound him, and kept him hidden.

sentences.zh: 戰方酣，使牽以過陳前，噪曰：「已獲李密矣！」

translations.literal: As the fighting grew fierce he had the man led before the ranks and shouted, "Li Mi has already been captured!"
translations.idiomatic: At the height of battle he had the man dragged before the lines and cried, "Li Mi is taken!"

sentences.zh: 士卒皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The soldiers all cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: His men roared in triumph.

sentences.zh: 其伏兵發，乘高而下，馳壓密營，縱火焚其廬舍。

translations.literal: His ambush troops sprang forth, swept down from the heights, galloped over Mi's camp, and set fire to the huts.
translations.idiomatic: His ambush burst from the heights, overran Mi's camp, and set the shelters ablaze.

sentences.zh: 密眾大潰，其將張童仁、陳智略皆降，密與萬餘人馳向洛口。

translations.literal: Mi's host broke in great disorder; his generals Zhang Tongren and Chen Zhilue both surrendered, and Mi fled with more than ten thousand men toward Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's army collapsed; generals Zhang Tongren and Chen Zhilue surrendered, and Mi fled toward Luokou with more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世充夜圍偃師；

translations.literal: Shichong by night besieged Yanshi;
translations.idiomatic: That night Shichong besieged Yanshi;

sentences.zh: 鄭頲守偃師，其部下翻城納世充。

translations.literal: Zheng Ting held Yanshi, but his subordinates turned the walls and admitted Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ting held the city, but his own men opened the gates to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 初，世充家屬在江都，隨宇文化及至滑台，又隨王軌入李密，密留於偃師，欲以招世充。

translations.literal: Earlier Shichong's family had been at Jiangdu; they followed Yu Wenhuaji to Huatai, then followed Wang Gui into Li Mi's camp; Mi kept them at Yanshi, intending to use them to win Shichong over.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shichong's family had been at Jiangdu, followed Yu Wenhuaji to Huatai, then Wang Gui into Li Mi's camp; Mi had kept them at Yanshi as hostages to win Shichong over.

sentences.zh: 及偃師破，世充得其兄世偉、子玄應、虔恕、瓊等，又獲密將佐裴仁基、鄭頲、祖君彥等數十人。

translations.literal: When Yanshi fell, Shichong recovered his elder brother Shiwei, his sons Xuanying, Qianshu, and Qiong, and also captured several dozen of Mi's officers and staff including Pei Renji, Zheng Ting, and Zu Junyan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshi fell, Shichong recovered his brother Shiwei, his sons Xuanying, Qianshu, and Qiong, and captured dozens of Mi's officers including Pei Renji, Zheng Ting, and Zu Junyan.

sentences.zh: 世充於是整兵向洛口，得邴元真妻子、鄭虔象母及密諸將子弟，皆撫慰之，令潛呼其父兄。

translations.literal: Shichong thereupon marshaled his troops toward Luokou; he obtained the wives and children of Bing Yuanzhen, the mother of Zheng Qianxiang, and the sons and younger brothers of Mi's generals, comforted them all, and had them secretly call out to their fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong then marched on Luokou; he took the families of Bing Yuanzhen, Zheng Qianxiang's mother, and the sons and brothers of Mi's generals, treated them kindly, and had them call out to their kin in secret.

sentences.zh: 初，邴元真為縣吏，坐贓亡命，從翟讓於瓦岡；

translations.literal: Initially Bing Yuanzhen had been a county clerk; convicted of embezzlement he fled as an outlaw and followed Zhai Rang at Wagang;
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuanzhen had once been a county clerk; convicted of graft he fled and joined Zhai Rang at Wagang;

sentences.zh: 讓以其嘗為吏，使掌書記。

translations.literal: Rang, because he had once been an official, put him in charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: Rang, knowing he had clerical experience, made him keep the records.

sentences.zh: 及密開幕府，妙選時英，讓薦元真為長史；

translations.literal: When Mi opened his headquarters and chose the finest men of the age, Rang recommended Yuanzhen as Chief Administrator;
translations.idiomatic: When Mi opened his headquarters and picked the best talent of the day, Rang recommended Yuanzhen as chief administrator;

sentences.zh: 密不得已用之，行軍謀畫，未嘗參預。

translations.literal: Mi used him only because he had to; in campaign planning he never took part.
translations.idiomatic: Mi used him only because he had to; Yuanzhen never had a hand in military planning.

sentences.zh: 密西拒世充，留元真守洛口倉。

translations.literal: Mi went west to hold off Shichong and left Yuanzhen to guard the Luokou granary.
translations.idiomatic: Mi marched west against Shichong and left Yuanzhen to guard the Luokou granary.

sentences.zh: 元真性貪鄙，宇文溫謂密曰：「不殺元真，必為公患。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was greedy and base; Yu Wenwen said to Mi, "If you do not kill Yuanzhen, he will surely become your scourge."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was greedy and corrupt; Yu Wenwen told Mi, "If you do not kill Yuanzhen, he will ruin you."

sentences.zh: 密不應。

translations.literal: Mi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Mi ignored him.

sentences.zh: 元真知之，陰謀叛密；

translations.literal: Yuanzhen learned of this and secretly plotted to betray Mi;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen learned of this and secretly plotted to defect;

sentences.zh: 楊慶聞之，以告密，密固疑焉。

translations.literal: Yang Qing heard of it and told Mi, who already harbored suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing heard and told Mi, who already suspected him.

sentences.zh: 至是，密將入洛口城，元真已遣人潛引世充矣。

translations.literal: At this point, as Mi was about to enter Luokou city, Yuanzhen had already sent men secretly to bring Shichong in.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as Mi was about to enter Luokou, Yuanzhen had already sent men to let Shichong in.

sentences.zh: 密知而不發，因與眾謀，待世充兵半濟洛水，然後擊之。

translations.literal: Mi knew but did not reveal it; he consulted his officers and planned to wait until half of Shichong's army had crossed the Luo River, then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Mi knew but said nothing; he planned with his officers to strike when half of Shichong's army was mid-crossing on the Luo.

sentences.zh: 世充軍至，密候騎不時覺，比將出戰，世充軍悉已濟矣。

translations.literal: When Shichong's army arrived, Mi's scouts did not report in time; by the time he was ready to give battle, Shichong's entire force had already crossed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong arrived, Mi's scouts failed to warn him in time; by the time Mi moved to fight, every man had crossed.

sentences.zh: 單雄信等又勒兵自據；

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin and others also marshaled troops and held their own ground;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin and others also held their troops apart;

sentences.zh: 密自度不能支，帥麾下輕騎奔虎牢，元真遂以城降。

translations.literal: Mi judged he could not hold out, led his light cavalry in flight to Hulao, and Yuanzhen thereupon surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mi saw he could not hold, fled with his light cavalry to Hulao, and Yuanzhen surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 初，雄信驍捷，善用馬槊，名冠諸軍，軍中號曰「飛將」。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiongxin had been fierce and swift, skilled with the cavalry lance, his fame foremost in all the armies; the troops called him the "Flying General."
translations.idiomatic: Xiongxin was fierce and swift with the cavalry lance, the finest fighter in the army; his men called him the Flying General.

sentences.zh: 彥藻以雄信輕於去就，勸密除之；

translations.literal: Yanzao, because Xiongxin was light in his loyalty, urged Mi to remove him;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzao, seeing how lightly Xiongxin shifted allegiance, urged Mi to kill him;

sentences.zh: 密愛其才，不忍也。

translations.literal: Mi valued his talent and could not bear to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi prized his talent and would not.

sentences.zh: 及密失利，雄信遂以所部降世充。

translations.literal: "When Mi met defeat, Xiongxin thereupon led his command in surrender to Shichong."
translations.idiomatic: "When Mi fell, Xiongxin took his troops over to Shichong."

sentences.zh: 密將如黎陽，或曰：「殺翟讓之際，徐世勣幾死，今失利而就之，安可保乎！」

translations.literal: Mi was about to go to Liyang when someone said, "When Zhai Rang was killed, Xu Shiji nearly died; now that you are defeated, if you go to him, how can you be safe!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi was heading for Liyang when someone warned, "When you killed Zhai Rang, Xu Shiji nearly died with him — now that you are beaten, how can you trust him?"

sentences.zh: 時王伯當棄金墉保河陽，密自虎牢歸之，引諸將共議。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and held Heyang; Mi returned to him from Hulao and gathered the generals for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and held Heyang; Mi joined him from Hulao and called his generals to council.

sentences.zh: 密欲南阻河，北守太行，東連黎陽，以圖進取。

translations.literal: Mi wished to block the river on the south, hold the Taihang range on the north, and link with Liyang on the east to plan further advances.
translations.idiomatic: Mi wanted to hold the Yellow River in the south, the Taihang Mountains in the north, and link with Liyang in the east for a new offensive.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「今兵新失利，眾心危懼，若更停留，恐叛亡不日而盡。

translations.literal: The generals all said, "Our army has just suffered defeat and hearts are fearful; if we linger further, I fear desertion will consume us within days.
translations.idiomatic: The generals said, "We have just been beaten and the men are terrified — linger here and they will desert within days.

sentences.zh: 又人情不願，難以成功。」

translations.literal: Moreover men's wishes do not incline that way — success will be hard."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the men do not want this plan — it cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「孤所恃者眾也，眾既不願，孤道窮矣。」

translations.literal: Mi said, "What I rely on is the multitude; if the multitude will not have it, my road is at an end."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "My strength is you — if you will not follow, I am finished."

sentences.zh: 欲自刎以謝眾。

translations.literal: He was about to cut his own throat to answer to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 伯當抱密號絕，眾皆悲泣，密復曰：「諸君幸不相棄，當共歸關中；

translations.literal: Bodang embraced him and wailed; all wept, and Mi said again, "If you will not abandon me, let us go together to Guanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Bodang seized him and wept; all wept with them. Mi said, "If you will not leave me, let us go to Guanzhong together;

sentences.zh: 密身雖無功，諸君必保富貴。」

translations.literal: though I myself have no merit left, you will surely keep wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: though I have no merit left, you will still win wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 府掾柳燮曰：「明公與唐公同族，兼有疇昔之好；

translations.literal: Staff officer Liu Xie said, "My lord shares clan with the Duke of Tang and has old friendship besides;
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Liu Xie said, "You are kin to the Duke of Tang and old friends besides;

sentences.zh: 雖不陪起兵，然阻東都，斷隋歸路，使唐公不戰而據長安，此亦公之功也。」

translations.literal: though you did not join in raising arms, you blocked the Eastern Capital and cut off Sui's road home, letting the Duke of Tang take Chang'an without fighting — this too is your merit."
translations.idiomatic: you did not march with him, but you pinned the Eastern Capital and cut Sui's retreat, letting the Duke of Tang take Chang'an without a battle — that is your merit too."

sentences.zh: 眾鹹曰：「然。」

translations.literal: All said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: All agreed."

sentences.zh: 密又謂王伯當曰：「將軍室家重大，豈復與孤俱行哉！」

translations.literal: Mi also said to Wang Bodang, "General, your household is weighty — how can you still travel with me!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi told Wang Bodang, "General, you have a great household — you need not come with me!"

sentences.zh: 伯當曰：「昔蕭何盡帥子弟以從漢王，伯當恨不兄弟俱從，豈以公今日失利遂輕去就乎！

translations.literal: Bodang said, "In old times Xiao He led all his sons and younger brothers to follow the King of Han; I regret that my brothers did not all come with me — how could I lightly leave you now that you have met defeat!
translations.idiomatic: Bodang said, "Xiao He once led all his kin to follow the King of Han — I regret my brothers are not all here; how could I abandon you because you have lost a battle!

sentences.zh: 縱身份原野，亦所甘心！」

translations.literal: Even if my body lies on the wild plain, I am content!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I die on the open field, I am content!"

sentences.zh: 左右莫不感激，從密入關者凡二萬人。

translations.literal: None present was unmoved; those who followed Mi into Guanzhong numbered twenty thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: All were moved; twenty thousand men followed Mi into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 於是密之將帥、州縣多降於隋。

translations.literal: Thereupon many of Mi's generals and prefectures and counties submitted to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Mi's generals and local officials then went over to Sui.

sentences.zh: 朱粲亦遣使降隋，皇泰主以粲為楚王。

translations.literal: Zhu Can also sent envoys to submit to Sui; Emperor Huangtai appointed Can Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can also sent envoys to submit; Emperor Huangtai made him Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，秦州總管竇軌擊薛仁果，不利；

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Dou Gui, overall commander of Qin Prefecture, attacked Xue Renguo without success;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin, Dou Gui, commander of Qin Prefecture, attacked Xue Renguo and was beaten;

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍劉感鎮涇州，仁果圍之。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Liu Gan held Jing Prefecture, and Renguo besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry General Liu Gan held Jing Prefecture, and Renguo besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，感殺所乘馬以分將士，感一無所啖，唯煮馬骨取汁和木屑食之。

translations.literal: When grain in the city was exhausted, Gan killed his own mount to share with the officers and men; he himself ate nothing but boiled the horse bones for broth mixed with wood shavings.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran out, Gan killed his own horse to feed his men; he ate nothing himself but boiled the bones for broth mixed with sawdust.

sentences.zh: 城垂陷者數矣，會長平王叔良將士至涇州，仁果乃揚言食盡，引兵南去；

translations.literal: The city was on the verge of falling several times; then Prince of Changping Shuliang arrived at Jing with troops, and Renguo proclaimed his food was gone and led his army south;
translations.idiomatic: The city nearly fell several times; then Prince Shuliang of Changping reached Jing with reinforcements, and Renguo claimed his food was gone and marched south;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，又遣高址人偽以城降。

translations.literal: on the day yimao he again sent men of Gaozhi to feign surrender of the city.
translations.idiomatic: on the day yimao he sent men from Gaozhi to fake a surrender.

sentences.zh: 叔良遣感帥眾赴之，己未，至城下，扣城中人曰：「賊已去，可逾城入。」

translations.literal: Shuliang sent Gan to lead troops thither; on the day jiwei they reached the city wall and called to those inside, "The bandits have gone — you may climb over the wall and enter."
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang sent Gan with troops; on the day jiwei they reached the wall and called, "The rebels are gone — come over the wall."

sentences.zh: 感命燒其門，城上下水灌之。

translations.literal: Gan ordered the gate burned; those on the wall poured water down.
translations.idiomatic: Gan ordered the gate burned; defenders poured water from above.

sentences.zh: 感知其詐，遣步兵先還，自帥精兵為殿。

translations.literal: Gan perceived the trickery, sent the foot soldiers back first, and himself led the crack troops as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Gan saw the trap, sent the infantry back first, and led the elite as rearguard himself.

sentences.zh: 俄而城上舉三烽，仁果兵自南原大下，戰於百里細川，唐軍大敗，感為仁果所擒。

translations.literal: Soon three beacon fires rose on the wall; Renguo's troops swept down from the southern heights, and at Baili Xichuan the Tang army was routed; Gan was captured by Renguo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon three signal fires rose; Renguo's men poured from the southern heights; at Baili Xichuan the Tang army was crushed and Gan was taken.

sentences.zh: 仁果復圍涇州，令感語城中云：「援軍已敗，不如早降。」

translations.literal: Renguo again besieged Jing Prefecture and had Gan tell the city, "Relief has been defeated — better surrender soon."
translations.idiomatic: Renguo besieged Jing again and ordered Gan to tell the city, "Your relief is destroyed — surrender now."

sentences.zh: 感許之，至城下，大呼曰：「逆賊饑餒，亡在朝夕，秦王帥數十萬眾，四面俱集，城中勿優，勉之！」

translations.literal: Gan agreed; at the wall he shouted, "The rebels are starving and will perish within days! The Prince of Qin leads hundreds of thousands gathering on every side — do not grieve in the city, take heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Gan agreed; at the wall he shouted, "The rebels are starving — they will die within days! Prince of Qin is coming with hundreds of thousands from every side — hold fast, take heart!"

sentences.zh: 仁果怒，執感，於城旁埋之至膝，馳騎射之；

translations.literal: Renguo in rage seized Gan, buried him to the knees beside the wall, and had horsemen ride past shooting him;
translations.idiomatic: Renguo in fury seized him, buried him to the knees by the wall, and had riders shoot him as they galloped past;

sentences.zh: 至死，聲色逾厲。

translations.literal: until death his voice and bearing grew only fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: until he died his voice never weakened.

sentences.zh: 叔良嬰城固守，僅能自全。

translations.literal: Shuliang held the city and defended stubbornly, barely preserving himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang held the walls and barely survived.

sentences.zh: 感，豐生之孫也。

translations.literal: Gan was the grandson of Fengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was the grandson of Liu Fengsheng.

sentences.zh: 庚申，隴州刺史陝人常達擊薛仁果於宜祿川，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Chang Da of Shaan, prefect of Long Prefecture, attacked Xue Renguo at Yilu River and took more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengshen, Chang Da of Shaan, prefect of Long, attacked Xue Renguo at Yilu River and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 上遣從子襄武公琛、太常卿鄭元□以女妓遺始畢可汗。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent his nephew the Duke of Xiangwu Chen and the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zheng Yuanshu to present female entertainers to the Shibi Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent his nephew Duke of Xiangwu Li Chen and Director Zheng Yuanshu with female entertainers as gifts to the Shibi Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，始畢復遣骨咄祿特勒來。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Shibi again sent the Tegin Kutlug.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renxu, Shibi sent the Tegin Kutlug again.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，白馬道士傅仁均造《戊寅歷》成，奏上，行之。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, the White Horse Daoist Fu Renjun completed the Wuyin Calendar, presented it to the throne, and it was put into use.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, the Daoist Fu Renjun of White Horse completed the Wuyin Calendar; it was submitted and adopted.

sentences.zh: 薛仁果屢攻常達，不能克，乃遣其將仵士政以數百人詐降，達厚撫之。

translations.literal: Xue Renguo repeatedly attacked Chang Da but could not overcome him; he therefore sent his general Wu Shizheng with several hundred men to feign surrender, and Da treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Renguo attacked Chang Da again and again without success; he sent General Wu Shizheng with several hundred men to fake a surrender, and Da welcomed them warmly.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，士政伺隙以其徒劫達，擁城中二千人降於仁果。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Shizheng seized an opening, with his followers seized Da, and leading two thousand men in the city surrendered to Renguo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, Shizheng seized his chance, overpowered Da, and led two thousand men in the city over to Renguo.

sentences.zh: 達見仁果，詞色不屈，仁果壯而釋之。

translations.literal: When Da was brought before Renguo his words and bearing did not bend; Renguo admired him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Brought before Renguo, Da would not bend; Renguo admired his spirit and let him go.

sentences.zh: 奴賊帥張貴謂達曰：「汝識我乎？」

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, leader of the slave-bandits, said to Da, "Do you know me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, a rebel chieftain, asked Da, "Do you know me?"

sentences.zh: 達曰：「汝逃死奴賊耳！」

translations.literal: Da said, "You are nothing but a runaway slave-bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: Da said, "You are a runaway slave rebel, nothing more!"

sentences.zh: 貴怒，欲殺之，人救之，獲免。

translations.literal: Gui in anger wished to kill him; others rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Gui in rage tried to kill him; others intervened and Da was spared.

sentences.zh: 辛未，追謚隋太上皇為煬帝。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, the retired Sui emperor was posthumously titled Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, the retired Sui sovereign was posthumously titled Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及至魏縣，張愷等謀去之；

translations.literal: When Yu Wenhuaji reached Wei County, Zhang Kai and others plotted to leave him;
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Wenhuaji reached Wei County, Zhang Kai and others plotted to abandon him;

sentences.zh: 事覺，化及殺之。

translations.literal: the plot was discovered and Huaji killed them.
translations.idiomatic: the plot was discovered and Huaji had them killed.

sentences.zh: 腹心稍盡，兵勢日蹙，兄弟更無他計，但相聚酣宴，奏女樂。

translations.literal: His close confidants were gradually exhausted and his military strength daily pressed; the brothers had no other plan but to gather for heavy drinking and female music.
translations.idiomatic: His inner circle dwindled and his army shrank daily; the brothers had no plan left but to drink together and listen to women's music.

sentences.zh: 化及醉，尤智及曰：「我初不知，由汝為計，強來立我。

translations.literal: When drunk Huaji blamed Zhiji, saying, "At first I did not know — it was your plan that forced the throne on me.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Huaji blamed Zhiji: "I never wanted this — you forced the throne on me.

sentences.zh: 今所向無成，士馬日散，負弒君之名，天下所不容。

translations.literal: Now nothing succeeds, troops and horses scatter daily, and I bear the name of regicide — the world will not tolerate me.
translations.idiomatic: Now we achieve nothing, our men scatter daily, and I bear the name of regicide — the world will not have me.

sentences.zh: 今者滅族，豈不由汝乎！」

translations.literal: Our clan's destruction now — is it not because of you!"
translations.idiomatic: Our whole clan will be destroyed — and it is your fault!"

sentences.zh: 持其兩子而泣。

translations.literal: He embraced his two sons and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He hugged his two sons and wept.

sentences.zh: 智及怒曰：「事捷之日，初不賜尤，及其將敗，乃欲歸罪，何不殺我以降竇建德！」

translations.literal: Zhiji angrily said, "When things went well you never blamed me; now that defeat nears you wish to lay guilt on me — why not kill me and surrender to Dou Jiande!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji snapped, "When we were winning you never blamed me — now that we are losing you blame me? Kill me and surrender to Dou Jiande!"

sentences.zh: 數相鬥鬩，言無長幼；

translations.literal: They quarreled repeatedly, with no regard for seniority;
translations.idiomatic: They quarreled constantly with no respect for rank;

sentences.zh: 醒而復飲，以此為恆。

translations.literal: sobering they drank again — this became their constant way.
translations.idiomatic: sobering up they drank again — that was their routine.

sentences.zh: 其眾多亡，化及自知必敗，歎曰：「人生固當死，豈不一日為帝乎！」

translations.literal: Many of their followers deserted; Huaji knew he must fail and sighed, "Men must die in the end — was it not worth being emperor for a single day!"
translations.idiomatic: Their men deserted in droves; Huaji knew he was finished and sighed, "A man must die — was one day as emperor not worth it!"

sentences.zh: 於是鴆殺秦王浩，即皇帝位於魏縣，國號許，改元天壽，署置百官。

translations.literal: He then poisoned Prince of Qin Hao, declared himself emperor at Wei County, named his state Xu, changed the era to Tianshou, and installed the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: He poisoned Prince of Qin Yang Hao, declared himself emperor at Wei County, named his state Xu, adopted the era Tianshou, and set up a full court.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: on the first day of the month, renshen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day renshen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，宴突厥骨咄祿，引骨咄祿升御坐以寵之。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin the Emperor feasted the Turk Kutlug, bringing Kutlug up to the imperial seat to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin the Emperor feasted the Turk Kutlug and seated him on the imperial dais as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 李密將至，上遣使迎勞，相望於道。

translations.literal: As Li Mi was about to arrive, the Emperor sent envoys to welcome and comfort him; they met one another all along the road.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Mi approached, the Emperor sent envoys to welcome him; their parties met all along the road.

sentences.zh: 密大喜，謂其徒曰：「我擁眾百萬，一朝解甲歸唐，山東連城數百，知我在此，遣使招之，亦當盡至；

translations.literal: Mi was greatly pleased and told his followers, "I once commanded a million men; in a single morning I laid down arms and returned to Tang. Hundreds of linked cities in Shandong, learning I am here, will send envoys to summon them — they too will all come;
translations.idiomatic: Mi was delighted and told his men, "I once led a million men; now I lay down my arms for Tang in a day. Hundreds of cities in Shandong will send for their lords once they know I am here — they will all come;

sentences.zh: 比於竇融，功亦不細，豈不以一台司見處乎！」

translations.literal: compared with Dou Rong my merit is not slight — surely I shall be treated with a seat among the Three Excellencies!"
translations.idiomatic: my merit is no less than Dou Rong's — surely they will give me a seat among the Three Excellencies!"

sentences.zh: 己卯，至長安，有司供待稍薄，所部兵累日不得食，眾心頗怨。

translations.literal: On the day jimao he reached Chang'an; the responsible offices provided rather meager hospitality, and his troops went without food for days — hearts in the ranks grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao he reached Chang'an; the court's hospitality was thin, and his men went hungry for days — morale soured.

sentences.zh: 既而以密為光祿卿、上柱國，賜爵邢國公。

translations.literal: Thereafter Mi was made Director of the Imperial Household, Pillar of the State, First Rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was then made Director of the Imperial Household, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Xing.

sentences.zh: 密既不滿望，朝臣又多輕之，執政者或來求賄，意甚不平；

translations.literal: Mi was dissatisfied with his rewards; many courtiers also looked down on him, and those in power sometimes came seeking bribes — his heart was very bitter;
translations.idiomatic: Mi was disappointed; courtiers looked down on him and officials came seeking bribes — he grew bitter;

sentences.zh: 獨上親禮之，常呼為弟，以舅子獨孤氏妻之。

translations.literal: only the Emperor treated him with personal honor, often calling him younger brother, and gave him a wife from the Dugu clan, his wife's kin.
translations.idiomatic: only the Emperor honored him personally, called him younger brother, and gave him a wife from the Dugu clan, kin of the Empress.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔右翊衛大將軍淮安王神通為山東道安扶大使，山東諸軍並受節度；

translations.literal: On the day gengchen an edict appointed Li Shentong, Prince of Huai'an, Grand General of the Right Yuyi Guard, as Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of the Shandong Circuit; all armies in Shandong were placed under his command;
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen the court named Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, Grand General of the Right Yuyi Guard, Pacification Commissioner for Shandong, with command over all armies there;

sentences.zh: 以黃門侍郎崔民幹為副。

translations.literal: Cui Mingan, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, was made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mingan, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, was his deputy.

sentences.zh: 鄧州刺史呂子臧與撫慰使馬元規擊朱粲，破之。

translations.literal: Lü Zizang, prefect of Deng Prefecture, and the Comfort Commissioner Ma Yuangui attacked Zhu Can and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zizang, prefect of Deng, and Comfort Commissioner Ma Yuangui attacked Zhu Can and beat him.

sentences.zh: 子臧言於元規曰：「粲新敗，上下危懼，請並力擊之，一舉可滅。

translations.literal: Zizang said to Yuangui, "Can has just been defeated and high and low are in fear — let us strike together and destroy him in one blow.
translations.idiomatic: Zizang urged Yuangui, "Can is freshly beaten and his men are terrified — strike together and we can finish him in one blow.

sentences.zh: 若復遷延，其徒稍集，力強食盡，致死於我，為患方深。」

translations.literal: If we delay further, his followers will gradually gather, his strength grow and his food run out — then he will fight us to the death and the harm will be grave indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Delay, and his men will regroup; when they are strong and starving they will fight us to the death — the danger will be far worse."

sentences.zh: 元規不從。

translations.literal: Yuangui would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui refused.

sentences.zh: 子臧請獨以所部兵擊之，元規不許。

translations.literal: Zizang asked to attack with his own troops alone; Yuangui did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zizang asked to attack with his own troops; Yuangui forbade it.

sentences.zh: 既而粲收集餘眾，兵復大振，自稱楚帝於冠軍，改元昌達，進攻鄧州。

translations.literal: Before long Can gathered his scattered forces, his army revived in strength, styled himself Emperor of Chu at Guanjun, changed the era to Changda, and advanced to attack Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Can soon rallied his remnants, revived his army, declared himself Emperor of Chu at Guanjun, adopted the era Changda, and marched on Deng.

sentences.zh: 子臧撫膺謂元規曰：「老夫今坐公死矣！」

translations.literal: Zizang beat his breast and said to Yuangui, "This old man will die because of you!"
translations.idiomatic: Zizang clutched his chest and told Yuangui, "I will die because of you!"

sentences.zh: 粲圍南陽，會霖雨城壞，所親勸子臧降。

translations.literal: Can besieged Nanyang; heavy rains came and the walls collapsed; those close to Zizang urged him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Can besieged Nanyang; rains collapsed the walls, and his intimates urged Zizang to surrender.

sentences.zh: 子臧曰：「安有天子方伯降賊者乎！」

translations.literal: Zizang said, "How could an imperial commissioner of the Son of Heaven surrender to bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Zizang said, "How could an imperial commissioner surrender to rebels!"

sentences.zh: 帥麾下赴敵而死。

translations.literal: He led his followers out to meet the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men out to fight and was killed.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，元規亦死。

translations.literal: Soon the city fell and Yuangui also died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell and Yuangui died as well.

sentences.zh: 癸未，王世充收李密美人珍寶及將卒十餘萬人還東都，陳於闕下。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Wang Shichong gathered Li Mi's beauties, treasures, and more than a hundred thousand officers and soldiers and returned to the Eastern Capital, displaying them below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, Wang Shichong brought Li Mi's concubines, treasure, and more than a hundred thousand troops back to the Eastern Capital and paraded them below the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，皇泰主大赦。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Emperor Huangtai proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, Emperor Huangtai proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以世充為太尉、尚書令，內外諸軍事，仍使之開太尉府，備置官屬，妙選人物。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Shichong was appointed Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, with authority over all military affairs internal and external; he was also allowed to open a Grand Commandant's office, fully staff it, and choose outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu, Shichong was made Grand Commandant and Director of the Masters of Writing with full military authority, allowed to open a commandant's office, staff it fully, and pick the best talent.

sentences.zh: 世充以裴仁基父子驍勇，深禮之。

translations.literal: Shichong, because Pei Renji and his sons were fierce and brave, treated them with deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong honored Pei Renji and his sons for their fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 徐文遠復入東都，見世充，必先拜。

translations.literal: Xu Wenyuan again entered the Eastern Capital; whenever he saw Wang Shichong, he always bowed first.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Wenyuan returned to the Eastern Capital, he always bowed first upon meeting Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「君倨見李密而敬王公，何也？」

translations.literal: Someone asked: "You were arrogant when you saw Li Mi yet deferential to the Prince of Zheng—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "Why did you treat Li Mi with arrogance but show respect to the Prince of Zheng?"

sentences.zh: 文遠曰：「魏公，君子也，能容賢士；

translations.literal: Wenyuan said: "The Duke of Wei is a gentleman who can accommodate worthy men;
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan replied, "The Duke of Wei is a gentleman who welcomes men of talent;

sentences.zh: 王公，小人也，能殺故人，吾何敢不拜！」

translations.literal: the Prince of Zheng is a petty man who can kill old friends—how could I dare not bow!"
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Zheng is a small man who will kill old friends. How could I dare not bow to him!"

sentences.zh: 李密總管李育德以武陟來降，拜陟州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Mi's general Li Yude surrendered with Wuzhi and was appointed Prefect of Buzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yude, a general under Li Mi, surrendered with Wuzhi and was appointed prefect of Buzhou.

sentences.zh: 育德，諤之孫也。

translations.literal: Yude was the grandson of Nie.
translations.idiomatic: Yude was a grandson of Nie.

sentences.zh: 其餘將佐劉德威、賈閏甫、高季輔等，或以城邑，或帥眾，相繼來降。

translations.literal: The other generals and aides—Liu Dewei, Jia Runpu, Gao Jifu, and the like—surrendered one after another, some with cities, others leading troops.
translations.idiomatic: His other officers and aides—Liu Dewei, Jia Runpu, Gao Jifu, and others—surrendered in succession, some bringing cities and others leading their troops.

sentences.zh: 初，北海賊帥綦公順帥其徒三萬攻郡城，已克其外郭，進攻子城；

translations.literal: At first the Beihai bandit chief Qi Gongshun led his thirty thousand followers to attack the commandery seat. He had already taken the outer city and was pressing the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Beihai bandit leader Qi Gongshun had led thirty thousand men to attack the commandery seat. Having already seized the outer city, he was pressing the attack on the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，公順自謂克在旦夕，不為備。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted. Gongshun thought capture was a matter of days and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: With food inside the city exhausted, Gongshun assumed victory was only days away and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 明經劉蘭成糾合城中驍健百餘人襲擊之，城中見兵繼之，公順大敗，棄營走，郡城獲全。

translations.literal: Liu Lancheng, holder of the classics degree, rallied more than a hundred of the city's fiercest fighters and struck them. When the garrison saw the attack, troops sallied to follow up. Gongshun suffered a great defeat, abandoned his camp, and fled, and the commandery seat was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lancheng, a classics-degree holder, gathered more than a hundred of the city's bravest men and launched a surprise attack. Seeing this, the garrison sallied in support. Gongshun was routed, abandoned his camp, and fled, and the commandery seat was saved.

sentences.zh: 於是郡官及望族分城中民為六軍，各將之，蘭成亦將一軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commandery officials and leading clans divided the city's people into six armies, each leader commanding one. Lancheng also commanded one army.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery officials and prominent families then divided the city's population into six armies, each under its own commander. Lancheng was given command of one army as well.

sentences.zh: 有宋書佐者，離間諸軍曰：「蘭成得眾心，必為諸人不利，不如殺之。」

translations.literal: There was a secretarial assistant named Song who sowed discord among the armies, saying: "Lancheng has won the hearts of the troops. He will surely bring harm to all of you. Better to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: A secretarial assistant named Song stirred division among the armies, saying, "Lancheng has won the soldiers' loyalty. He will surely work against us all. We had better kill him."

sentences.zh: 眾不忍殺，但奪其兵以授宋書佐。

translations.literal: The troops could not bring themselves to kill him but only stripped him of his soldiers and gave them to Assistant Song.
translations.idiomatic: The men could not bring themselves to kill him, but they stripped him of his troops and handed command to Assistant Song.

sentences.zh: 蘭成恐終及禍，亡奔公順。

translations.literal: Lancheng, fearing he would eventually come to disaster, fled and joined Gongshun.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that disaster would catch up with him in the end, Lancheng fled and joined Gongshun.

sentences.zh: 公順軍中喜噪，欲奉以為主，固辭，乃以為長史，軍事鹹聽焉。

translations.literal: Gongshun's army rejoiced and clamored, wishing to make him their leader. He firmly declined and was then made Chief Clerk; all military affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshun's army erupted in joy and clamor, wanting to make Lancheng their leader. He firmly refused, and was instead appointed chief clerk, with all military affairs left to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 居五十餘日，蘭成簡軍中驍健者百五十人，往抄北海。

translations.literal: After more than fifty days, Lancheng selected a hundred and fifty of the army's fiercest warriors and went to raid Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: After fifty-odd days, Lancheng picked a hundred and fifty of the army's toughest fighters and set out to raid Beihai.

sentences.zh: 距城四十里，留十人，使多芟草，分為百餘積；

translations.literal: Forty li from the city he left ten men and had them cut much grass and pile it in more than a hundred heaps.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li from the city he posted ten men and had them cut large amounts of grass and stack it in more than a hundred piles.

sentences.zh: 二十里，又留二十人，各執大旗；

translations.literal: At twenty li he left another twenty men, each holding a large banner.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty li he posted another twenty men, each carrying a large banner.

sentences.zh: 五六里，又留三十人，伏險要；

translations.literal: At five or six li he left thirty more men in ambush at a strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six li out he posted thirty more men in ambush at a defensible spot.

sentences.zh: 蘭成自將十人，夜，距城一里許潛伏；

translations.literal: Lancheng personally led ten men and, at night, hid about one li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lancheng himself led ten men and, under cover of night, lay in wait about one li from the city.

sentences.zh: 余八十人分置便處，約聞鼓聲即抄取人畜亟去，仍一時焚積草。

translations.literal: The remaining eighty he posted at convenient points, agreeing that on hearing the drum they would seize people and livestock and leave at once, and at the same time set the piled grass ablaze.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining eighty he distributed at advantageous points, with orders that at the sound of the drum they were to seize people and livestock and withdraw immediately, while at the same time setting the grass piles afire.

sentences.zh: 明晨，城中遠望無煙塵，皆出樵牧。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, looking far from the city and seeing no dust or smoke, everyone went out to gather firewood and herd.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, seeing no dust or smoke in the distance, the people of the city all went out to cut wood and tend their herds.

sentences.zh: 日向中，蘭成以十人直抵城門，城上鉦鼓亂髮；

translations.literal: When the sun neared midday, Lancheng with ten men drove straight to the city gate; on the walls gongs and drums sounded in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Near midday, Lancheng led ten men straight to the city gate, and gongs and drums on the walls sounded in wild alarm.

sentences.zh: 伏兵四出，抄掠雜畜千餘頭及樵牧者而去。

translations.literal: Ambushers burst out on all sides, seized more than a thousand mixed livestock plus wood-cutters and herdsmen, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ambush parties sprang out on every side, drove off more than a thousand head of mixed livestock along with woodcutters and herdsmen, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蘭成度抄者已遠，徐步而還。

translations.literal: Lancheng judged the raiders were already far off and walked back at an unhurried pace.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that the raiders were already well away, Lancheng walked back at a leisurely pace.

sentences.zh: 城中雖出兵，恐有伏兵，不敢急追；

translations.literal: Though the city sent troops out, they feared ambushes and did not dare pursue hotly.
translations.idiomatic: Although the city sent troops out, they feared further ambushes and did not dare pursue aggressively.

sentences.zh: 又見前有旌旗、煙火，遂不敢進而還。

translations.literal: Seeing banners and signal fires ahead, they dared not advance and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When they also saw banners and signal fires ahead, they dared not press forward and turned back.

sentences.zh: 既而城中知蘭成前者眾少，悔不窮追。

translations.literal: Soon the city learned that Lancheng's advance party had been few in number and regretted not having pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city learned that Lancheng's advance force had been small in number, and they regretted not having pursued to the finish.

sentences.zh: 居月餘，蘭成謀取郡城，更以二十人直抵城門。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Lancheng plotted to take the commandery seat and again sent twenty men straight to the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: After another month or so, Lancheng planned to seize the commandery seat and once more sent twenty men straight to the city gate.

sentences.zh: 城中人競出逐之，行未十里，公順將大軍總至。

translations.literal: The townspeople rushed out to chase them. Before they had gone ten li, Gongshun arrived at the head of the main force.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople rushed out to pursue them, but before they had gone ten li, Gongshun arrived at the head of the main army.

sentences.zh: 郡兵奔馳還城，公順進兵圍之，蘭成一言招諭，城中人爭出降。

translations.literal: The commandery troops raced back to the city. Gongshun advanced and besieged it. With a single appeal Lancheng won them over, and the people competed to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery soldiers raced back into the city. Gongshun advanced and laid siege, and with a single summons Lancheng persuaded the people to submit; they competed to come out and surrender.

sentences.zh: 蘭成撫存老幼，禮遇郡官，見宋書佐，亦禮之如舊，仍資送出境，內外安堵。

translations.literal: Lancheng comforted the old and young, treated the commandery officials with courtesy, and when he saw Assistant Song likewise received him as before, provisioned him and sent him beyond the border. Within and without, all was settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Lancheng cared for the old and young, treated the commandery officials with courtesy, and when he met Assistant Song received him with the same respect as before, then supplied him and escorted him beyond the border. Within and without, all was calm and secure.

sentences.zh: 時海陵賊帥臧君相聞公順據北海，帥其眾五萬來爭之；

translations.literal: At this time the bandit chief Zang Junxiang of Hailing, hearing that Gongshun held Beihai, led his fifty thousand followers to contest it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zang Junxiang, the bandit leader of Hailing, heard that Gongshun held Beihai and led fifty thousand men to contest the region.

sentences.zh: 公順眾少，聞之大懼。

translations.literal: Gongshun's forces were few, and hearing this he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshun's forces were few, and when he heard this he was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 蘭成為公順畫策曰：「君相今去此尚遠，必不為備，請將軍倍道襲擊其營。」

translations.literal: Lancheng devised a plan for Gongshun, saying: "Junxiang is still far from here and surely unprepared. I ask you, General, to take a forced march and strike his camp."
translations.idiomatic: Lancheng devised a plan for Gongshun, saying, "Junxiang is still far from here and surely will not be on guard. General, please take a forced march and strike his camp."

sentences.zh: 公順從之，自將驍勇五千人，繼熟食，倍道襲之。

translations.literal: Gongshun agreed. He personally led five thousand picked warriors, ate cooked food on the march, and made a forced march to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshun agreed. He personally led five thousand elite troops, ate cooked rations on the march, and made a forced march to raid the enemy.

sentences.zh: 將至，蘭成與敢死士二十人前行，距君相營五十里，見其抄者負擔向營，蘭成亦與其徒負擔蔬米、燒器，詐為抄者，擇空而行聽察，得其號及主將姓名；

translations.literal: As they neared, Lancheng went ahead with twenty death-defying volunteers. Fifty li from Junxiang's camp they saw his foragers carrying loads toward camp. Lancheng and his men too shouldered vegetables, grain, and cooking utensils, disguised themselves as foragers, chose empty routes to walk and listen, and learned the passwords and the chief commander's name.
translations.idiomatic: As they drew near, Lancheng went ahead with twenty volunteers willing to die. Fifty li from Junxiang's camp they saw enemy foragers carrying loads back toward camp. Lancheng and his men shouldered vegetables, grain, and cooking gear, disguised themselves as foragers, chose empty paths while listening and observing, and learned the watchwords and the commander's name.

sentences.zh: 至暮，與賊比肩而入，負擔巡營，知其虛實，得其更號。

translations.literal: At dusk they entered shoulder to shoulder with the enemy, carrying loads and walking through the camp, learning its strengths and weaknesses and obtaining the watchword.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk they entered the camp shoulder to shoulder with the enemy, carrying loads and walking through the lines until they knew the camp's strengths and weaknesses and had learned the watchword.

sentences.zh: 乃於空地燃火營食，至三鼓，忽於主將幕前交刀亂下，殺百餘人，賊眾驚擾；

translations.literal: Then in an open space they lit fires and made camp meals. At the third watch they suddenly crossed blades in front of the commander's tent and struck down more than a hundred men; the enemy troops were alarmed and thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: They then lit fires in an open space and cooked their meal. At the third watch they suddenly crossed blades in front of the commander's tent and cut down more than a hundred men, throwing the enemy camp into panic and confusion.

sentences.zh: 公順兵亦至，急攻之，君相僅以身免，俘斬數千，收其資糧甲仗以還。

translations.literal: Gongshun's troops also arrived and pressed the attack fiercely. Junxiang barely escaped with his life. They captured and slew several thousand, gathered their supplies, grain, and armor, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshun's troops also arrived and pressed the attack. Junxiang barely escaped with his life. They captured and killed several thousand men, seized their supplies, grain, and armor, and returned.

sentences.zh: 由是公順黨眾大盛。

translations.literal: From this Gongshun's following greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: From this Gongshun's following grew greatly in strength.

sentences.zh: 及李密據洛口，公順以眾附之，密敗，亦來降。

translations.literal: When Li Mi held Luokou, Gongshun joined him with his forces. After Mi was defeated, he also came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi held Luokou, Gongshun joined him with his troops. After Li Mi's defeat, he too came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 隋末群盜起，冠軍司兵李襲譽說西京留守陰世師遣兵據永豐倉，發粟以賑窮乏，出庫物賞戰士，移檄郡縣，同心討賊；

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, when bandits rose everywhere, Li Xiyu, a clerk in the Champion Office, urged the Western Capital's defender Yin Shishi to send troops to hold the Yongfeng granary, release grain to relieve the destitute, distribute goods from the stores to reward warriors, and issue proclamations to commanderies and counties to unite in suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, when bandits rose on every side, Li Xiyu, a clerk in the Champion Office, urged Yin Shishi, defender of the Western Capital, to send troops to seize the Yongfeng granary, release grain to relieve the poor, distribute stores to reward fighting men, and issue proclamations to the commanderies and counties calling on them to unite against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 世師不能用。

translations.literal: Shishi would not adopt the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi would not accept the proposal.

sentences.zh: 乃求募兵山南，世師許之。

translations.literal: He then requested permission to raise troops south of the mountains; Shishi granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked permission to raise troops south of the mountains, and Shishi granted it.

sentences.zh: 上克長安，自漢中召還，為太府少卿；

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozu took Chang'an, he was recalled from Hanzhong and made Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu captured Chang'an, Xiyu was recalled from Hanzhong and appointed Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 乙未，附襲譽籍於宗正。

translations.literal: On the day yimi, Xiyu's name was entered in the registers of the Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimi, Xiyu's name was entered in the registers of the Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 襲譽，襲志之弟也。

translations.literal: Xiyu was the younger brother of Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyu was the younger brother of Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 丙申，朱粲寇淅州，遣太常卿鄭元□帥步騎一萬擊之。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Zhu Can raided Xizhou. The court sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu at the head of ten thousand foot and horse to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingshen, Zhu Can raided Xizhou. The court dispatched Grand Master of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu at the head of ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him.

sentences.zh: 是月，納言竇抗罷為左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: That month, Grand Counselor Dou Kang was removed from office and made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That month Grand Counselor Dou Kang was removed from office and appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙巳，涼王李軌即皇帝位，改元安樂。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day yisi, Li Gui, King of Liang, assumed the imperial title and changed the era name to Anle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day yisi, Li Gui, King of Liang, declared himself emperor and adopted the era name Anle.

sentences.zh: 戊申，王軌以滑州來降。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Wang Gui surrendered with Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen, Wang Gui came over in surrender with Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 薛仁果之為太子也，與諸將多有隙；

translations.literal: When Xue Renguo was crown prince, he had many rifts with the generals.
translations.idiomatic: While Xue Renguo was still crown prince, he had many quarrels with his generals.

sentences.zh: 及即位，眾心猜懼。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, everyone's hearts were suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, the army's hearts were filled with suspicion and fear.

sentences.zh: 郝瑗哭舉得疾，遂不起，由是國勢浸弱。

translations.literal: Hao Yuan took ill from weeping at the enthronement and never recovered; from this the state's power gradually weakened.
