translations.idiomatic: Hao Yuan fell ill from grief at the enthronement and never recovered, and from that point the state's strength steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民至高址，仁果使宗羅□將兵拒之；

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Li Shimin reached Gaozhi. Renguo sent Zong Luohou to command troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Li Shimin advanced to Gaozhi. Renguo sent Zong Luohou to command troops against him.

sentences.zh: 羅□侯數挑戰，世民堅壁不出。

translations.literal: Luohou repeatedly challenged to battle; Shimin held his walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou repeatedly offered battle, but Shimin held his fortifications and refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 諸將鹹請戰，世民曰：「我軍新敗，士氣沮喪，賊恃勝而驕，有輕我心，宜閉壘以待之。

translations.literal: All the generals begged for battle. Shimin said: "Our army has just been defeated; morale is crushed. The enemy, trusting in victory, is arrogant and looks down on us. We should shut the walls and wait them out.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals begged to fight. Shimin said, "Our army has just suffered defeat and morale is low. The enemy, emboldened by victory, is arrogant and underestimates us. We should hold our defenses and wait.

sentences.zh: 彼驕我奮，可一戰而克也。」

translations.literal: When they are arrogant and we are roused, we can defeat them in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: When they are arrogant and we are roused, we can defeat them in one battle."

sentences.zh: 乃令軍中曰：「敢言戰者斬！」

translations.literal: He then ordered the army: "Whoever speaks of fighting shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an order throughout the army: "Whoever speaks of giving battle shall be executed!"

sentences.zh: 相持六十餘日，仁果糧盡，其將梁胡郎等帥所部來降。

translations.literal: They faced off for more than sixty days. Renguo's grain ran out; his generals Liang Hulu and others led their units to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They faced each other for more than sixty days. Renguo's grain ran out, and his generals Liang Hulu and others led their units over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 世民知仁果將士離心，命行軍總管梁實營於淺水原以誘之。

translations.literal: Shimin knew Renguo's officers and men were divided in heart and ordered Acting Grand Marshal Liang Shi to camp on the Qianshui Plain as bait.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Renguo's officers and men were losing heart, Shimin ordered Acting Grand Marshal Liang Shi to encamp on the Qianshui Plain as bait.

sentences.zh: 羅□侯大喜，盡銳攻之，梁實守險不出；

translations.literal: Luohou was greatly delighted and attacked with his full elite force; Liang Shi held the defile and would not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou was overjoyed and attacked with his full elite strength, but Liang Shi held the defensible ground and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 營中無水，人馬不飲者數日。

translations.literal: There was no water in the camp; men and horses went without drinking for days.
translations.idiomatic: There was no water in the camp, and men and horses went without drink for days.

sentences.zh: 羅□侯攻之甚急；

translations.literal: Luohou pressed the attack fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou pressed the attack with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 世民度賊已疲，謂諸將曰：「可以戰矣！」

translations.literal: Shimin judged the enemy were exhausted and told the generals: "We can fight now!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin judged that the enemy were exhausted and told his generals, "We can fight now!"

sentences.zh: 遲明，使右武候大將軍寵玉陳於淺水原。

translations.literal: At dawn he had Grand General of the Right Martial Guard Pang Yu deploy on the Qianshui Plain.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he had Grand General of the Right Martial Guard Pang Yu draw up his line on the Qianshui Plain.

sentences.zh: 羅□侯並兵擊之，玉戰，幾不能支，世民引大軍自原北出其不意，羅□侯引兵還戰。

translations.literal: Luohou combined his forces and struck him. Yu fought and nearly could not hold; Shimin led the main army from the north of the plain to take them unawares, and Luohou turned his troops to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou combined his forces and attacked. Yu fought hard and nearly could not hold the line. Shimin then led the main army from the north of the plain to take the enemy by surprise, and Luohou wheeled his troops around to meet him.

sentences.zh: 世民帥驍騎數十先陷陳，唐兵表裡奮擊，呼聲動地。

translations.literal: Shimin himself led dozens of fierce cavalry to break the enemy line first; Tang troops struck from front and rear with all their might, and their shouts shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin himself led several dozen elite horsemen to break the enemy line first. Tang troops struck from front and rear with all their strength, and their battle cries shook the ground.

sentences.zh: 羅□侯士卒大潰，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Luohou's soldiers collapsed in great disorder; several thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou's soldiers broke in complete rout, and several thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 世民帥二千餘騎追之，竇軌叩馬苦諫曰：「仁果猶據堅城，雖破羅□侯，未可輕進，請且按兵以觀之。」

translations.literal: Shimin led more than two thousand cavalry in pursuit. Dou Gui grasped his horse's bridle and pleaded earnestly: "Renguo still holds a strong city. Though we have broken Luohou, we must not advance rashly. I beg you to hold the army back and observe."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin led more than two thousand cavalry in pursuit. Dou Gui seized his horse's bridle and pleaded urgently, "Renguo still holds a strong city. Though we have defeated Luohou, we must not advance rashly. Please hold the army back and wait to see what happens."

sentences.zh: 世民曰「吾慮之久矣，破竹之勢，不可失也，舅勿復言！」

translations.literal: Shimin said: "I have long considered this. The momentum of splitting bamboo cannot be lost. Uncle, say no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said, "I have thought about this for a long time. The momentum of splitting bamboo cannot be lost. Uncle, say no more!"

sentences.zh: 遂進。

translations.literal: He pressed on.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 仁果陳於城下，世民據涇水臨之，仁果驍將渾幹等數人臨陳來降。

translations.literal: Renguo drew up his line below the city. Shimin took position along the Jing River facing him. Renguo's fierce generals Hun Gan and several others came before the battle line to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Renguo drew up his battle line below the city. Shimin took position along the Jing River and faced him. Several of Renguo's fierce generals, including Hun Gan, came before the lines to surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁果懼，引兵入城拒守。

translations.literal: Renguo was afraid and withdrew his troops into the city to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Renguo was frightened and withdrew his troops into the city to hold out.

sentences.zh: 日向暮，大軍繼至，遂圍之。

translations.literal: As the sun set, the main army arrived and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: As the sun was setting, the main army arrived and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 夜半，守城者爭自投下。

translations.literal: At midnight, defenders competed to throw themselves down from the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the defenders competed to throw themselves down from the walls in surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁果計窮，己酉，出降；

translations.literal: Renguo's plans were exhausted. On the day jiyou he came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: With no options left, Renguo came out and surrendered on the day jiyou.

sentences.zh: 得其精兵萬餘人，男女五萬口。

translations.literal: They obtained more than ten thousand elite soldiers and fifty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than ten thousand elite soldiers and fifty thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆賀，因問曰：「大王一戰而勝，遽捨步兵，又無攻具，輕騎直造城下，眾皆以為不克，而卒取之，何也？」

translations.literal: All the generals offered congratulations and then asked: "Your Highness, after winning one battle you abruptly left the infantry behind, had no siege equipment, and with light cavalry rode straight to the city walls. Everyone thought you could not take it, yet in the end you did—why?"
translations.idiomatic: All the generals offered congratulations and then asked, "Your Highness, after winning one battle you abruptly abandoned the infantry, had no siege equipment, and with light cavalry rode straight to the city walls. Everyone thought you could not take it, yet in the end you did. Why?"

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「羅□侯所將皆隴外之人，將驍卒悍；

translations.literal: Shimin said: "Those Luohou commanded were all people from beyond Long—bold officers and fierce soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said, "The men Luohou commanded were all people from beyond Long—bold commanders and fierce soldiers;

sentences.zh: 吾特出其不意而破之，斬獲不多。

translations.literal: we struck them by surprise and broke them, but the kills and captures were not many.
translations.idiomatic: we broke them by surprise, but the kills and captures were not many.

sentences.zh: 若緩之，則皆入城，仁果撫而用之，未易克也；

translations.literal: If we had delayed, they would all have entered the city. Renguo would have comforted and employed them, and it would not have been easy to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If we had delayed, they would all have entered the city. Renguo would have reassured and employed them, and the city would not have been easy to take;

sentences.zh: 急之，則散歸隴外。

translations.literal: If we pressed hard, they would scatter back beyond Long.
translations.idiomatic: if we pressed hard, they would scatter back beyond Long.

sentences.zh: 折址虛弱，仁果破膽，不暇為謀，此吾所以克也。」

translations.literal: Zhezhi was hollow and weak; Renguo's heart was broken and he had no leisure to plot—this is why we could take it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhezhi was hollow and weak, Renguo's courage was broken, and he had no time to devise a plan. That is why we were able to take it."

sentences.zh: 眾皆悅服。

translations.literal: All were pleased and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: All were pleased and convinced.

sentences.zh: 世民所得降卒，悉使仁果兄弟及宗羅□侯、翟長孫等將之，與之射獵，無所疑間。

translations.literal: The surrendered soldiers Shimin had taken he put entirely under the command of Renguo's brothers and Zong Luohou, Zhai Changsun, and the like, hunting with them without the slightest distrust.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin put all the surrendered soldiers under the command of Renguo's brothers, Zong Luohou, Zhai Changsun, and the like, and went hunting with them without the slightest suspicion.

sentences.zh: 賊畏威銜恩，皆願效死。

translations.literal: The enemy, awed by his might and grateful for his kindness, all wished to die in his service.
translations.idiomatic: Awed by his authority and grateful for his kindness, the former enemy soldiers all wished to die in his service.

sentences.zh: 世民聞褚亮名，求訪，獲之，禮遇甚厚，引為王府文學。

translations.literal: Shimin had heard of Chu Liang's reputation, sought him out, and obtained him. He treated him with great honor and appointed him literary aide to the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin had heard of Chu Liang's reputation, sought him out, and found him. He treated him with great honor and appointed him literary aide to the princely household.

sentences.zh: 上遣使謂世民曰：「薛舉父子多殺我士卒，必盡誅其黨以謝冤魂。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent a messenger to tell Shimin: "The Xue father and son killed many of our soldiers. You must execute their entire faction to appease the wronged dead."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent a messenger to tell Shimin, "The Xue father and son killed many of our soldiers. You must execute their entire faction to appease the wronged dead."

sentences.zh: 李密諫曰：「薛舉虐殺不辜，此其所以亡也，陛下何怨焉？

translations.literal: Li Mi remonstrated: "Xue Ju's slaughter of the innocent is precisely why he perished. Why should Your Majesty harbor resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi remonstrated, "Xue Ju's slaughter of the innocent is precisely why he perished. Why should Your Majesty bear a grudge?

sentences.zh: 懷服之民，不可不撫。」

translations.literal: The people who submit in their hearts must not go unappeased."
translations.idiomatic: The people who submit in their hearts must be reassured."

sentences.zh: 乃命戮其謀首，余皆赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the ringleaders of the plot executed and pardoned the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered the chief plotters executed and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 上使李密迎秦王世民於豳州，密自恃智略功名，見上猶有傲色；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent Li Mi to welcome Prince of Qin Li Shimin at Binzhou. Mi, trusting in his wit, strategy, and achievements, still showed an air of pride when he saw the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent Li Mi to welcome Prince of Qin Li Shimin at Binzhou. Confident in his wit, strategy, and past achievements, Mi still showed an air of pride when he met the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 及見世民，不覺驚服，私謂殷開山曰：「真英主也！

translations.literal: When he saw Shimin, he was involuntarily struck and subdued. Privately he told Yin Kaishan: "A true hero-emperor!
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Shimin, he was involuntarily awed and subdued. Privately he told Yin Kaishan, "A true hero-emperor!

sentences.zh: 不如是，何以定禍亂乎！」

translations.literal: If not such a man, how could the calamities and disorders be settled!"
translations.idiomatic: If not such a man, how could the chaos and disorder ever be settled!"

sentences.zh: 詔以員外散騎常侍姜謨為秦州刺史，謨撫以恩信，盜賊悉歸首，士民安之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jiang Mo, Acting Palace Attendant and Cavalier Attendant, Prefect of Qinzhou. Mo governed with kindness and trust; bandits all surrendered themselves, and officials and commoners were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Jiang Mo, Acting Palace Attendant and Cavalier Attendant, as prefect of Qinzhou. Mo governed with kindness and trust; bandits all surrendered themselves, and officials and commoners lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 徐世勣據李密舊境，未有所屬。

translations.literal: Xu Shiji held Li Mi's former territory and had not yet declared allegiance to anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji held Li Mi's former territory and had not yet pledged allegiance to anyone.

sentences.zh: 魏徵隨密至長安，乃自請安集山東，上以為秘書丞，乘傳至黎陽，遺徐世勣書，勸之早降。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng followed Mi to Chang'an, then himself requested to pacify and settle Shandong; Emperor Gaozu appointed him Secretary of the Palace Library; riding relay horses he reached Liyang, sent a letter to Xu Shiji, and urged him to submit early.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng had followed Li Mi to Chang'an; he now volunteered to pacify Shandong. Emperor Gaozu made him secretary of the palace library and sent him by relay post to Liyang with a letter urging Xu Shiji to surrender at once.

sentences.zh: 世勣遂決計西向，謂長史陽翟郭孝恪曰：「此眾土地，皆魏公有也；

translations.literal: Shiji then resolved to turn west and said to Chief Administrator Guo Xiaoke of Yangdi: "These troops and lands all belong to the Duke of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Shiji then decided to turn west. He told his chief administrator, Guo Xiaoke of Yangdi, "These forces and these lands all belong to the Duke of Wei;

sentences.zh: 吾若上表獻之，是利主之敗，自為功以邀富貴也，吾實恥之。

translations.literal: if I submit a memorial offering them up, it would be profiting from my lord's defeat and making merit for myself to win wealth and rank — I am truly ashamed of that.
translations.idiomatic: If I sent a memorial offering them up myself, I would be profiting from my lord's defeat and claiming the credit for wealth and rank. I am ashamed of that.

sentences.zh: 今宜籍郡縣戶口士馬之數以啟魏公，使自獻之。」

translations.literal: Now we ought to register the numbers of households, population, troops, and horses in each commandery and county and report them to the Duke of Wei, so that he himself may offer them up."
translations.idiomatic: The right course is to tally the households, population, troops, and horses of every commandery and county and report them to the Duke of Wei, so that he himself may make the submission."

sentences.zh: 乃遣孝恪詣長安，又運糧以餉淮安王神通。

translations.literal: He then sent Xiaoke to Chang'an and also shipped grain to supply Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiaoke to Chang'an and shipped grain to supply Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong.

sentences.zh: 上聞世勣使者至，無表，止有啟與密，甚怪之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu heard that Shiji's envoy had arrived with no memorial but only a report to Mi, he was much puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu learned that Shiji's envoy had come with no formal memorial—only a private report to Li Mi—he was much puzzled.

sentences.zh: 孝恪具言世勣意，上乃歎曰：「徐世勣不背德，不邀功，真純臣也！」

translations.literal: Xiaoke fully explained Shiji's intent; Emperor Gaozu then sighed and said, "Xu Shiji does not betray virtue and does not claim merit for himself — a truly pure-hearted minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoke explained Shiji's intent in full. Emperor Gaozu sighed and said, "Xu Shiji neither betrays his obligations nor grabs credit for himself—a loyal minister in the truest sense!"

sentences.zh: 賜姓李。

translations.literal: He granted him the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 以孝恪為宋州刺史，使與世勣經營虎牢以東，所得州縣，委之選補。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiaoke prefect of Song Prefecture and had him join Shiji in administering east of Hulao; commanderies and counties taken were entrusted to them for appointments and filling posts.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xiaoke prefect of Song Prefecture and had him work with Shiji to administer everything east of Hulao; whatever commanderies and counties they took, the two men were empowered to appoint officials and fill posts.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，獨孤懷恩攻堯君素於蒲板。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Dugu Huai'en attacked Yao Junsu at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Dugu Huai'en attacked Yao Junsu at Puban.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管趙慈景尚帝女桂陽公主，為君素所擒，梟首城外，以示無降意。

translations.literal: Marching-general Zhao Cijing had married the Emperor's daughter Princess Guiyang; he was captured by Junsu, whose men displayed his head outside the walls to show they had no intention of surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: The marching-general Zhao Cijing had married the Emperor's daughter, Princess Guiyang. Yao Junsu captured him and had his head displayed outside the walls to show that he would not surrender.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，秦王世民至長安，斬薛仁果於市，上賜常達帛三百段。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Prince of Qin Li Shimin reached Chang'an and executed Xue Renguo in the marketplace; Emperor Gaozu granted Chang Da three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Prince of Qin Li Shimin returned to Chang'an and had Xue Renguo executed in the marketplace. Emperor Gaozu rewarded Chang Da with three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 贈劉感平原郡公，謚忠壯。

translations.literal: Liu Gan was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan, with the posthumous name Loyal and Bold.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gan was posthumously made Duke of Pingyuan, with the posthumous name Loyal and Bold.

sentences.zh: 撲殺仵士政於殿庭。

translations.literal: Wu Shizheng was beaten to death in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shizheng was beaten to death in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 以張貴尤淫暴，腰斬之。

translations.literal: Because Zhang Gui was especially lewd and cruel, he was executed by waist chop.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, notorious for lewdness and brutality, was cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 上享勞將士，因謂群臣曰：「諸公共相翊戴以成帝業，若天下承平，可共保富貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu feasted and thanked the officers and soldiers, then said to the assembled ministers, "You all have jointly supported and raised me to complete the imperial enterprise; if the realm is at peace, you may together preserve wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu feasted his officers and soldiers and then told his ministers, "You have all supported me and helped build this throne. When the realm is at peace, we may share its rewards.

sentences.zh: 使王世充得志，公等豈有種乎！

translations.literal: If Wang Shichong were to have his way, would any of you keep your seed alive!
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Shichong had his way, would any of you survive to leave heirs!

sentences.zh: 如薛仁果君臣，豈可不以為前鑒也！」

translations.literal: Like the lord and ministers of Xue Renguo — can you not take them as a warning!"
translations.idiomatic: Look at Xue Renguo and his followers — will you not take them as a warning!"

sentences.zh: 己巳，以劉文靜為戶部尚書，領陝東道行台左僕射，復殷開山爵位。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Liu Wenjing was appointed Minister of Revenue and Left Vice Director of the Eastern-Shaanxi Circuit headquarters; Yin Kaishan's noble rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Liu Wenjing was made Minister of Revenue and left vice director of the Eastern-Shaanxi Circuit headquarters, and Yin Kaishan's noble rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 李密驕貴日久，又自負歸國之功，朝廷待之不副本望，鬱鬱不樂。

translations.literal: Li Mi had long been proud of his exalted status; he also prided himself on his merit in returning to the dynasty, yet the court's treatment did not match his expectations, and he was gloomy and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had grown arrogant in his high station. He also took pride in having brought his forces back to the dynasty, yet the court treated him below what he expected, and he brooded in discontent.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇大朝會，密為光祿卿，當進食，深以為恥；

translations.literal: Once at a grand court assembly, Mi as Director of the Imperial Household was obliged to serve food — he deeply felt this shameful;
translations.idiomatic: At a grand court assembly, Mi, now Director of the Imperial Household, was assigned to serve food—a duty he found deeply humiliating;

sentences.zh: 退，以告左武衛大將軍王伯當。

translations.literal: on returning he told Left Martial Guards Commander Wang Bodang.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told Wang Bodang, commander of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 伯當心亦怏怏，因謂密曰：「天下事在公度內耳。

translations.literal: Bodang's heart was also discontent; he therefore said to Mi, "The affairs of the realm lie within your power alone.
translations.idiomatic: Bodang was equally discontent. He told Mi, "The fate of the realm is entirely in your hands.

sentences.zh: 今東海公在黎陽，襄陽公在羅口，河南兵馬，屈指可計，豈得久如此也！」

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Donghai is at Liyang and the Duke of Xiangyang at Luokou; the troops and horses of Henan can be counted on one's fingers — how can you remain like this for long!"
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Donghai is at Liyang and the Duke of Xiangyang at Luokou. Henan's armies are still at your command. How long can you endure this humiliation!"

sentences.zh: 密大喜，乃獻策於上曰：「臣虛蒙榮寵，安坐京師，曾無報效；

translations.literal: Mi was greatly pleased and then presented a plan to Emperor Gaozu, saying, "I have vainly received honor and favor yet sit idle in the capital with never a deed of service;
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Mi submitted a plan to Emperor Gaozu: "I have received honors I have not earned and sit idle in the capital without repaying them;

sentences.zh: 山東之眾皆臣故時麾下，請往收而撫之。

translations.literal: the masses of Shandong are all my former subordinates — I request permission to go gather and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Shandong are still my old followers. Let me go gather and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 憑藉國威，取王世充如拾地芥耳！」

translations.literal: Relying on the dynasty's majesty, taking Wang Shichong would be like picking up a mustard seed from the ground!"
translations.idiomatic: With the throne's authority behind me, taking Wang Shichong would be as easy as picking a seed off the ground!"

sentences.zh: 上聞密故將士多不附世充，亦欲遣密往收之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard that many of Mi's former generals and soldiers did not follow Shichung and also wished to send Mi to gather them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu knew that many of Mi's former followers still refused Wang Shichung and wanted to send Mi to win them back.

sentences.zh: 群臣多諫曰：「李密狡猾好反，今遣之，如投魚於泉，放虎於山，必不返矣！」

translations.literal: Many ministers remonstrated, saying, "Li Mi is crafty and prone to rebellion; if you send him now, it is like throwing a fish into a spring or releasing a tiger onto a mountain — he will surely not return!"
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers warned, "Li Mi is cunning and rebellion runs in his bones. Send him away now and it will be like throwing a fish back into the stream or a tiger back onto the mountain—he will never return!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「帝王自有天命，非小子所能取。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Emperors have their own mandate of Heaven — it is not something a petty man can seize.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu answered, "An emperor's mandate comes from Heaven—not something a lesser man can seize.

sentences.zh: 借使叛去，如以蒿箭射蒿中耳！

translations.literal: Even if he were to rebel and leave, it would be like shooting an artemisia arrow into an artemisia ear!
translations.idiomatic: Even if he did rebel and flee, it would be like shooting an arrow made of wormwood into a wormwood target!

sentences.zh: 今使二賊交鬥，吾可以坐收其弊。」

translations.literal: Now if I let the two bandits fight each other, I can sit and harvest the exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: Let the two rebels tear at each other, and I can reap the profit without stirring."

sentences.zh: 辛未，遣密詣山東，收其餘眾之未下者。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Mi was dispatched to Shandong to gather those of his remaining followers who had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he dispatched Li Mi to Shandong to gather the followers who had not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 密請與賈閏甫偕行，上許之，命密及閏甫同升御榻，賜食，傳飲卮酒曰：「吾三人同飲是酒，以明同心；

translations.literal: Mi requested to travel with Jia Runfu; Emperor Gaozu agreed, ordered Mi and Runfu together to ascend the imperial couch, granted them food, and passed them a cup of wine, saying, "We three drink this wine together to make our hearts one;
translations.idiomatic: Mi asked to take Jia Runfu with him. Emperor Gaozu agreed, had both men sit with him on the imperial couch, fed them, and passed them a cup of wine. "Let the three of us drink this together," he said, "as proof of shared purpose;

sentences.zh: 善建功名，以副朕意。

translations.literal: build merit and achieve fame to match my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Go and win glory worthy of my trust.

sentences.zh: 丈夫一言許人，千金不易。

translations.literal: A man, once he gives his word, will not change it for a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: A man's word, once given, is worth more than gold.

sentences.zh: 有人確執不欲弟行，朕推赤心於弟，非他人所能間也。」

translations.literal: Some obstinately did not wish you, my younger brother, to go; I lay my sincere heart before you, my younger brother — others cannot come between us."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged strongly against letting you go. I give you my open heart, and no one can come between us."

sentences.zh: 密、閏甫再拜受命。

translations.literal: Mi and Runfu bowed twice and accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Mi and Runfu bowed twice and accepted the commission.

sentences.zh: 上又以王伯當為密副而遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu also made Wang Bodang Mi's deputy and sent him along.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu also appointed Wang Bodang as Mi's deputy and sent them off together.

sentences.zh: 有大鳥五集於樂壽，群鳥數萬從之，經日乃去。

translations.literal: Five large birds alighted at Le Shou, and tens of thousands of birds followed them; after a full day they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Five great birds settled at Le Shou, followed by tens of thousands of smaller birds; after a full day they flew away.

sentences.zh: 竇建德以為己瑞，改元五鳳。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande took this as his own auspicious omen and changed the era name to Five Phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande took this as an omen in his favor and changed the era name to Five Phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 宗城人有得玄圭獻於建德者，宋正本及景城丞會稽孔德紹皆曰：「此天所以賜大禹也，請改國號曰夏。」

translations.literal: A man of Zongcheng obtained a black jade tablet and presented it to Jiande; Song Zhenben and Jing Prefecture assistant Kong Deshao of Kuaiji both said, "This is what Heaven gave Da Yu — we request that the state name be changed to Xia."
translations.idiomatic: A man of Zongcheng found a black jade scepter and presented it to Jiande. Song Zhenben and Assistant Magistrate Kong Deshao of Jing Prefecture in Kuaiji both said, "Heaven gave this to Great Yu. Change the state name to Xia."

sentences.zh: 建德從之，以正本為納言，德紹為內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Jiande followed this; he made Zhenben Director of the Secretariat and Deshao Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande agreed. He made Zhenben director of the secretariat and Deshao vice director of the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，王須拔掠幽州，中流矢死，其將魏刀兒代領其眾，據深澤，掠冀、定之間，眾至十萬，自稱魏帝。

translations.literal: Initially Wang Xuba raided You Prefecture, was struck by a stray arrow and died; his general Wei Dao'er took over his host, held Shenze, raided between Ji and Ding, and grew to one hundred thousand men, styling himself Emperor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuba had been raiding You Prefecture when he was killed by a stray arrow. His general Wei Dao'er took over the band, seized Shenze, and plundered between Ji and Ding until his force reached a hundred thousand. He styled himself Emperor of Wei.

sentences.zh: 建德偽與連和，刀兒弛備，建德襲擊破之，遂圍深澤；

translations.literal: Jiande feigned alliance with him; Dao'er relaxed his guard; Jiande launched a surprise attack and routed him, then besieged Shenze;
translations.idiomatic: Jiande pretended to ally with him. Dao'er let down his guard; Jiande struck by surprise, broke his force, and besieged Shenze;

sentences.zh: 其徒執刀兒降，建德斬之，盡並其眾。

translations.literal: his followers seized Dao'er and surrendered; Jiande beheaded him and fully absorbed his host.
translations.idiomatic: His men delivered Dao'er to Jiande in surrender. Jiande beheaded him and absorbed his entire following.

sentences.zh: 易、定等州皆降，唯冀州刺史麴稜不下，稜婿崔履行，暹之孫也，自言有奇術，可使攻者自敗，稜信之。

translations.literal: Yi, Ding, and other prefectures all submitted; only Qu Ling, prefect of Ji Prefecture, did not yield. Ling's son-in-law Cui Lüxing, grandson of Xianzhi, claimed to have strange arts by which attackers would defeat themselves, and Ling trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Ding, and the other prefectures submitted. Only Ji Prefecture's governor Qu Ling held out. Ling's son-in-law Cui Lüxing, grandson of Xianzhi, claimed occult arts that would make attackers destroy themselves, and Qu Ling believed him.

sentences.zh: 履行命守城者皆坐，毋得妄鬥，曰：「賊雖登城，汝曹勿怖，吾將使賊自縛。」

translations.literal: Lüxing ordered the defenders all to sit and not fight recklessly, saying, "Though bandits climb the walls, you need not fear — I will make the bandits bind themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Lüxing ordered the defenders to sit still and not fight. "Even if the rebels reach the wall," he said, "do not be afraid. I will make them bind themselves."

sentences.zh: 於是為壇，夜，設章醮，然後自衣衰絰，杖竹登北樓慟哭；

translations.literal: He then built an altar; at night he performed Taoist rites, then himself put on mourning garments, took a bamboo staff, ascended the north tower, and wailed in grief;
translations.idiomatic: He built an altar and performed Taoist rites by night. Then he dressed in mourning, took up a bamboo staff, climbed the north tower, and wailed;

sentences.zh: 又令婦女升屋四向振裙。

translations.literal: he also had women climb onto rooftops and shake their skirts in all four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He also had women climb onto rooftops on all four sides and flutter their skirts.

sentences.zh: 建德攻之急，稜將戰，履行固止之。

translations.literal: Jiande pressed the attack hard; Ling was about to fight, but Lüxing firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande pressed the assault. Qu Ling wanted to fight, but Lüxing firmly forbade it.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，履行哭猶未已。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; Lüxing was still weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell—while Lüxing was still weeping.

sentences.zh: 建德見稜，曰：「卿忠臣也！」

translations.literal: Jiande saw Ling and said, "You are a loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande met Qu Ling, he said, "You are a loyal minister!"

sentences.zh: 厚禮之，以為內史令。

translations.literal: He treated him generously and made him Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande honored him and made him director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，詔以秦王世民為太尉、使持節、陝東道大行台，其蒲州、河北諸府兵馬並受節度。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renshen, an edict appointed Prince of Qin Li Shimin Grand Commander, Credential Bearer, and Grand Headquarters of the Eastern-Shaanxi Circuit; all troops of Pu Prefecture, Hebei, and other circuits were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen, an edict made Prince of Qin Li Shimin Grand Commander, Credential Bearer, and head of the Eastern-Shaanxi Circuit headquarters; all forces of Pu Prefecture, Hebei, and other circuits were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，西突厥曷娑那可汗自宇文化及所來降。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the Western Turk Qaghan Ashina Duojian submitted from Yu Wenhuaji's camp.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Western Turk qaghan Ashina Duojian came from Yu Wenhuaji's camp to submit.

sentences.zh: 隋將堯君素守河東，上遣呂紹宗、韋義節、獨孤懷恩相繼攻之，俱不下。

translations.literal: The Sui general Yao Junsu held Hedong; Emperor Gaozu sent Lü Shaozong, Wei Yijie, and Dugu Huai'en in succession to attack him, but none could take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui general Yao Junsu held Hedong. Emperor Gaozu sent Lü Shaozong, Wei Yijie, and Dugu Huai'en in succession to attack him, but none could take the city.

sentences.zh: 時外圍嚴急，君素為木鵝，置表於頸，具論事勢，浮之於河；

translations.literal: The siege outside was tight; Junsu made wooden geese, placed memorials on their necks fully stating the situation, and floated them on the river;
translations.idiomatic: The siege tightened. Junsu fashioned wooden geese, tied dispatches around their necks describing the situation, and floated them down the river;

sentences.zh: 河陽守者得之，達於東都。

translations.literal: the defenders at Heyang recovered them and forwarded them to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders at Heyang retrieved them and sent them to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主見而歎息，拜君素金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Huangtai saw them and sighed, appointing Junsu as Golden Beryl Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huangtai read them, sighed, and enfeoffed Junsu as Golden Beryl Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 寵玉、皇甫無逸自東都來降，上悉遣詣城下，為陳利害，君素不從。

translations.literal: Chong Yu and Huangfu Wuyi came from the Eastern Capital to submit; Emperor Gaozu sent them all to the foot of the walls to explain advantage and harm, but Junsu would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Yu and Huangfu Wuyi had surrendered from the Eastern Capital. Emperor Gaozu sent them to the walls to explain the stakes, but Junsu refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 又賜金券，許以不死。

translations.literal: He also granted a gilt warrant promising he would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted a gilt warrant promising that Junsu would not be executed.

sentences.zh: 其妻又至城下，謂之曰：「隋室已亡，君何自苦！」

translations.literal: His wife also came to the foot of the walls and said to him, "The house of Sui is already gone — why torment yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife came to the foot of the wall and called up, "The house of Sui is gone. Why torment yourself!"

sentences.zh: 君素曰：「天下名義，非婦人所知！」

translations.literal: Junsu said, "The great principles of the realm are not what a woman can understand!"
translations.idiomatic: Junsu answered, "The great principles of loyalty are not for women to judge!"

sentences.zh: 引弓射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: He drew his bow and shot her; she fell as the string sounded.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his bow and shot her down on the spot.

sentences.zh: 君素亦自知不濟，然志在守死，每言及國家，未嘗不歔欷。

translations.literal: Junsu also knew himself that success was unlikely, yet his intent was to hold to death; whenever he spoke of the state he never failed to sigh and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu knew he could not hold out forever, yet he meant to die defending the city. Whenever he spoke of the realm he wept.

sentences.zh: 謂將士曰：「吾昔事主上於籓邸，大義不得不死。

translations.literal: He told the officers and soldiers, "In former days I served the late emperor at the princely residence — the great principle demands that I must die.
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "I once served our late emperor at his princely residence. Honor demands that I die here.

sentences.zh: 必若隋祚永終，天命有屬，自當斷頭以付諸君，聽君等持取富貴。

translations.literal: If it must be that the fortune of Sui endures forever and Heaven's mandate has its destined recipient, then I should of myself cut off my head and hand it to you, letting you seek wealth and rank for yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: If Sui's mandate truly endures and Heaven has already chosen another, I will cut off my own head and let you take it to whoever holds the mandate and seek your reward.

sentences.zh: 今城池甚固，倉儲豐備，大事猶未可知，不可橫生心也！」

translations.literal: Now the walls are very strong and the granaries well stocked; the great outcome is still uncertain — you must not rashly turn disloyal!"
translations.idiomatic: Our walls are strong and our stores full. The outcome is still uncertain. Do not turn traitor in haste!"

sentences.zh: 君素性嚴明，善御眾，下莫敢叛。

translations.literal: Junsu by nature was strict and clear, skilled at commanding men; none below dared rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu was stern and disciplined, and ruled his men well. None dared rebel against him.

sentences.zh: 久之，倉粟盡，人相食；

translations.literal: After a long time the granary grain was exhausted and people ate one another;
translations.idiomatic: In time the granaries emptied and people ate one another;

sentences.zh: 又獲外人，微知江都傾覆。

translations.literal: they also captured outsiders and faintly learned of the catastrophe at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: They also captured an outsider and learned faint news of the disaster at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 丙子，君素左右薛宗、李楚客殺君素以降，傳首長安。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Junsu's attendants Xue Zong and Li Chuke killed Junsu to surrender; his head was sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Junsu's attendants Xue Zong and Li Chuke killed him and surrendered. His head was sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 君素遣朝散大夫解人王行本將精兵七百在它所，聞之，赴救，不及，因捕殺君素者黨與數百人，悉誅之，復乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Junsu had dispatched Palace Attendant Wang Xingben of Jie Prefecture at the head of seven hundred picked troops elsewhere; hearing of it, he rushed to rescue but could not arrive in time; he therefore seized the faction of those who killed Junsu, several hundred men, and executed them all, then again mounted the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu had posted Palace Attendant Wang Xingben of Jie with seven hundred elite troops elsewhere. Xingben rushed back but arrived too late. He seized several hundred accomplices in the murder, executed them all, and again mounted the walls to resist.

sentences.zh: 獨孤懷恩引兵圍之。

translations.literal: Dugu Huai'en led troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Huai'en brought troops to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，隋襄平太守鄧暠以柳城、北平二郡來降；

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Sui's Xiangping prefect Deng Hao came to submit with Liu Cheng and Beiping commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Sui's Xiangping prefect Deng Hao surrendered with the two commanderies of Liucheng and Beiping;

sentences.zh: 以暠為營州總管。

translations.literal: Hao was appointed area commander of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Hao was made area commander of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，太常卿鄭元□擊朱粲於商州，破之。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Grand Master of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu attacked Zhu Can at Shang Prefecture and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Grand Master of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu attacked Zhu Can at Shang Prefecture and routed him.

sentences.zh: 初，宇文化及遣使招羅藝，藝曰：「我，隋臣也！」

translations.literal: Initially Yu Wenhuaji sent envoys to win over Luo Yi; Yi said, "I am a minister of Sui!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Wenhuaji sent envoys to win over Luo Yi, Yi replied, "I am a minister of Sui!"

sentences.zh: 斬其使者，為煬帝發喪，臨三日。

translations.literal: He beheaded the envoys, held mourning rites for Emperor Yang, and mourned for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded the envoys, held mourning rites for Emperor Yang, and wept for three days.

sentences.zh: 竇建德、高開道各遣使招之，藝曰：「建德、開道，皆劇賊耳。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao each sent envoys to win him; Yi said, "Jiande and Kaidao are both fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao each sent envoys. Yi said, "Jiande and Kaidao are nothing but ferocious bandits.

sentences.zh: 吾聞唐公已定關中，人望歸之。

translations.literal: I hear the Duke of Tang has settled Guanzhong and the people's hopes turn to him.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Duke of Tang has secured Guanzhong and that men's hopes turn to him.

sentences.zh: 此真吾主也，吾將從之，敢沮議者，斬！」

translations.literal: This is truly my lord; I am going to follow him — whoever dares obstruct the plan, beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He is my true sovereign, and I mean to follow him. Whoever dissents—beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 會張道源慰撫山東，藝遂奉表，與漁陽、上谷等諸郡皆來降。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Daoyuan was pacifying Shandong; Yi then submitted a memorial, and Yuyang, Shanggu, and other commanderies all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daoyuan was then pacifying Shandong. Yi submitted his allegiance, and Yuyang, Shanggu, and the other commanderies followed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔以藝為幽州總管。

translations.literal: On the day guimou, an edict appointed Yi area commander of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guimou, an edict made Yi area commander of You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 薛萬均，世雄之子也，與弟萬徹俱以勇略為藝所親待，詔以萬均為上柱國、永安郡公，萬徹為車騎將軍、武安縣公。

translations.literal: Xue Wanjun was the son of Shixiong; he and his younger brother Wanche were both favored by Yi for courage and resource; an edict made Wanjun Grand Preceptor and Duke of Yong'an, and Wanche Cavalry General and Duke of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanjun, son of Shixiong, and his brother Wanche were both valued by Yi for courage and skill. Wanjun was made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Yong'an; Wanche was made Cavalry General and Duke of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 竇建德既克冀州，兵威益盛，帥眾十萬寇幽州。

translations.literal: After Dou Jiande had taken Ji Prefecture, his military prestige grew ever stronger; he led one hundred thousand men to raid You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande took Ji Prefecture his prestige and strength grew. He led a hundred thousand men against You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 藝將逆戰，萬均曰：「彼眾我寡，出戰必敗。

translations.literal: Yi was about to meet him in battle; Wanjun said, "They are many and we are few — if we fight we must lose.
translations.idiomatic: Yi prepared to meet him in battle. Wanjun said, "They outnumber us. We will lose if we go out to fight.

sentences.zh: 不若使羸兵背城阻水為陳，彼必渡水擊我。

translations.literal: Better to array weak troops with their backs to the city blocking the water — they will surely cross the river to strike us.
translations.idiomatic: Better to array our weaker troops with their backs to the city across the water. They will surely ford the river to attack.

sentences.zh: 萬均請以精騎百人伏於城旁，俟其半渡擊之，蔑不勝矣。」

translations.literal: Wanjun requested one hundred picked cavalry to lie in ambush beside the city; when the enemy was half across, strike them — none could fail to win."
translations.idiomatic: Let me take a hundred picked horsemen and lie in wait beside the city. Strike them halfway across and we cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 藝從之。

translations.literal: Yi followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yi agreed.

sentences.zh: 建德果引兵渡水，萬均邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Jiande indeed led troops across the water; Wanjun intercepted and routed them heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande forded the river as expected. Wanjun ambushed him and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 建德竟不能至其城下，乃分兵掠霍堡及雍奴等縣；

translations.literal: Jiande could not reach the city after all; he then divided his troops to raid Huobao and Yongnu and other counties;
translations.idiomatic: Jiande never reached the city. He split his force to plunder Huobao, Yongnu, and other counties;

sentences.zh: 藝復邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Yi again intercepted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ambushed him again and won.

sentences.zh: 凡相拒百餘日，建德不能克，乃還樂壽。

translations.literal: In all they resisted for more than a hundred days; Jiande could not take the place and then returned to Le Shou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred days Jiande still could not take Youzhou and withdrew to Le Shou.

sentences.zh: 藝得隋通直謁者溫彥博，以為司馬。

translations.literal: Yi obtained the Sui direct-attendant attendant Wen Yanbo and made him staff strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took the Sui direct-attendant Wen Yanbo and made him his military adviser.

sentences.zh: 藝以幽州歸國，彥博贊成之；

translations.literal: When Yi brought You Prefecture back to the dynasty, Yanbo supported and accomplished it;
translations.idiomatic: When Yi brought You Prefecture into the Tang fold, Yanbo urged and helped bring it about;

sentences.zh: 詔以彥博為幽州總管府長史，未幾，征為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yanbo chief administrator of the You Prefecture headquarters; before long he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was made chief administrator of the You Prefecture headquarters and soon afterward was recalled as vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 兄大雅，時為黃門侍郎，與彥博對居近密，時人榮之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Daya was then Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and lived opposite Yanbo close to the inner palace — men of the time envied them.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Daya was then vice director of the Yellow Gate; the two brothers lived opposite each other near the inner palace—a distinction men envied.

sentences.zh: 以西突厥曷娑那可汗為歸義王。

translations.literal: The Western Turk Qaghan Ashina Duojian was made Prince of Righteous Submission.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk qaghan Ashina Duojian was enfeoffed as Prince of Righteous Submission.

sentences.zh: 曷娑那獻大珠，上曰：「珠誠至寶；

translations.literal: Ashina Duojian presented a large pearl. Emperor Gaozu said, "The pearl is indeed a supreme treasure;
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Duojian offered a great pearl. Emperor Gaozu said, "The pearl is truly a treasure beyond price;

sentences.zh: 然朕寶王赤心，珠無所用。」

translations.literal: yet I treasure the king's loyal heart—the pearl is of no use to me."
translations.idiomatic: but I value your loyal heart, and the pearl is of no use to me."

sentences.zh: 竟還之。

translations.literal: In the end he returned it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he sent it back.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，車駕幸周氏陂，過故墅。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, the imperial carriage visited the Zhou family embankment and passed the old villa.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the Emperor traveled to the Zhou family embankment and passed his former estate.

sentences.zh: 初，羌豪旁企地以所部附薛舉，及薛仁果敗，企地來降，留長安，企地不樂，帥其眾數千叛，入南山，出漢川，所過殺掠。

translations.literal: Initially the Qiang chieftain Pang Qidi had attached his band to Xue Ju; when Xue Renguo was defeated, Qidi came to submit, was kept at Chang'an, was unhappy, led several thousand men in revolt, entered the Southern Mountains, emerged into Hanzhong, killing and plundering wherever he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Qiang chieftain Pang Qidi had joined Xue Ju with his followers. After Xue Renguo's defeat Qidi surrendered and was kept at Chang'an, but he was discontent; he led several thousand men in rebellion, entered the Southern Mountains, broke out into Hanzhong, and killed and looted all along his route.

sentences.zh: 武候大將軍寵玉擊之，為企地所敗。

translations.literal: Grand General of the Right Martial Guard Pang Yu attacked him and was defeated by Qidi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General of the Right Martial Guard Pang Yu attacked him and was beaten by Qidi.

sentences.zh: 行至始州，掠女子王氏，與俱醉臥野外；

translations.literal: When he reached Shi Prefecture he seized a woman of the Wang clan; drunk together they slept in the open country.
translations.idiomatic: At Shi Prefecture he seized a woman surnamed Wang; they drank together and slept drunk in the open fields.

sentences.zh: 王氏拔其佩刀，斬首送梁州，其眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Wang drew his belt knife, cut off his head, and sent it to Liang Prefecture; his followers then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang pulled his dagger, cut off his head, and sent it to Liang Prefecture; his band then broke apart.

sentences.zh: 詔賜王氏號崇義夫人。

translations.literal: An edict granted Wang the title Lady of Exalted Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict bestowed on Wang the title Lady of Exalted Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，王世充帥眾三萬圍谷州，刺史任瑰拒卻之。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Wang Shichong led thirty thousand men to besiege Gu Prefecture; the prefect Ren Gui repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Wang Shichong led thirty thousand troops to besiege Gu Prefecture, but Prefect Ren Gui drove him back.

sentences.zh: 上使李密分其麾下之半留華州，將其半出關。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Li Mi to leave half his followers at Hua Prefecture and lead the other half out through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had Li Mi leave half his troops at Hua Prefecture and march the other half out through the pass.

sentences.zh: 長史張寶德預在行中，恐密亡去，罪相及；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhang Baode was with the column and feared that if Mi fled, guilt would extend to him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhang Baode was traveling with the column and feared that if Mi absconded, he would be punished too.

sentences.zh: 上封事，言其必叛。

translations.literal: He submitted a sealed memorial to the Emperor saying Mi was certain to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Emperor a sealed memorial warning that Mi would surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 上意乃中變，又恐密驚駭，乃降敕書勞來，令密留所部徐行，單騎入朝，更受節度。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind then changed midway; fearing Mi would be alarmed, he issued an edict of consolation, ordering Mi to leave his troops to advance slowly while he alone rode to court to receive new orders.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu changed his mind midway but feared alarming Mi, so he issued a comforting edict ordering Mi to leave his troops to march slowly while he rode alone to court for reassignment.

sentences.zh: 密至稠桑，得敕，謂賈閏甫曰：「敕遣我去，無故復召我還，天子向雲，『有人確執不許』，此譖行矣。

translations.literal: When Mi reached Chousang and received the edict, he said to Jia Runfu, "The edict sent me away, then for no reason summons me back. When the Son of Heaven was wavering, 'someone firmly held that it should not be permitted'—slander has taken effect.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi reached Chousang and read the edict, he told Jia Runfu, "The edict sent me away, then for no reason calls me back. When the Son of Heaven was wavering, 'someone firmly insisted it must not be allowed'—slander has worked.

sentences.zh: 吾今若還，無復生理，不若破桃林縣，收其兵糧，北走渡河。

translations.literal: If I return now I have no chance of life. Better to overrun Taolin County, gather its arms and grain, flee north and cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: If I go back now I am as good as dead. Better to seize Taolin County, take its arms and grain, flee north, and cross the river.

sentences.zh: 比信達熊州，吾已遠矣。

translations.literal: By the time word reaches Xiong Prefecture I shall already be far away.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the report reaches Xiong Prefecture I will already be gone.

sentences.zh: 苟得至黎陽，大事必成。

translations.literal: If I can reach Liyang, the great enterprise will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: If I can reach Liyang, the great cause will surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 公意如何？」

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 閏甫曰：「主上待明公甚厚；

translations.literal: Runfu said, "Our lord has treated you, my lord, with great generosity;
translations.idiomatic: Runfu said, "Our lord has treated you with great kindness;

sentences.zh: 況國家姓名，著在圖讖，天下終當一統。

translations.literal: Moreover the dynastic surname is recorded in prognostic texts—the realm will in the end be united.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the dynasty's name is written in the prophecies—the realm will be united in the end.

sentences.zh: 明公既已委質，復生異圖，任瑰、史萬寶據熊、穀二州，此事朝舉，彼兵夕至，雖克桃林，兵豈暇集，一稱叛逆，誰復容人！

translations.literal: Since you have already pledged allegiance, to harbor another design—Ren Gui and Shi Wanbao hold Xiong and Gu prefectures; if this matter is raised at court their troops arrive by evening. Even if you take Taolin, where will troops be gathered in time? Once labeled rebel, who will shelter you!
translations.idiomatic: You have already pledged yourself to Tang; if you turn to another plan, Ren Gui and Shi Wanbao hold Xiong and Gu—raise this at court and their troops arrive by nightfall. Even if you take Taolin, where will you gather an army in time? Once you are called a rebel, who will take you in!

sentences.zh: 為明公計，不若且應朝命，以明元無異心，自然浸潤不行；

translations.literal: For your sake, better to obey the court for now, showing you harbor no other intent—then slander will naturally fail.
translations.idiomatic: For your own sake, better obey the court for now and show you mean no treachery—then the slander will die away.

sentences.zh: 更欲出就山東，徐思其便可也。」

translations.literal: If you still wish to go out to Shandong, consider the proper moment later."
translations.idiomatic: If you still want to go east to Shandong, you can think again when the time is right."

sentences.zh: 密怒曰：「唐使吾與絳、灌同列，何以堪之！

translations.literal: Mi raged, "Tang has placed me in the same rank as Zhou Bo and Guan Ying—how can I bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Mi flared up. "Tang ranks me with Zhou Bo and Guan Ying—how can I endure that!

sentences.zh: 且讖文之應，彼我所共。

translations.literal: And the fulfillment of the prophecy text—we share it between us.
translations.idiomatic: And the prophecy applies to both of us alike.

sentences.zh: 今不殺我，聽使東行，足明王者不死；

translations.literal: That they do not kill me but let me go east proves the destined king does not die.
translations.idiomatic: That they do not kill me but let me go east proves the man destined to rule does not die.

sentences.zh: 縱使唐遂定關中，山東終為我有。

translations.literal: Even if Tang settles Guanzhong, Shandong will in the end be mine.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Tang secures Guanzhong, Shandong will still be mine in the end.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，乃欲束手投人！

translations.literal: Heaven gives and I do not take—yet I would bind my hands and submit!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven offers and I refuse—only to bind my hands and surrender!

sentences.zh: 公，吾之心腹，何意如是！

translations.literal: You are my trusted confidant—how can you think so!
translations.idiomatic: You are my closest confidant—how can you speak like this!

sentences.zh: 若不同心，當斬而後行！」

translations.literal: If we are not of one mind, I shall cut you down before I go!"
translations.idiomatic: If we are not of one mind, I will cut you down before I move!"

sentences.zh: 閏甫泣曰：「明公雖雲應讖，近察天人，稍已相違。

translations.literal: Runfu wept, "Though you speak of fulfilling prophecy, on closer look heaven and men have already drifted apart.
translations.idiomatic: Runfu wept. "Though you speak of fulfilling the prophecy, look closely at heaven and men—they have already parted ways.

sentences.zh: 今海內分崩，人思自擅，強者為雄；

translations.literal: Now the realm is splitting apart—every man seeks to rule himself, the strong become lords.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is breaking apart; every man wants to rule himself, and the strong make themselves lords.

sentences.zh: 明公奔亡甫爾，誰相聽受！

translations.literal: You have only just become a fugitive—who will heed you!
translations.idiomatic: You have only just become a fugitive—who will listen to you!

sentences.zh: 且自翟讓受戮之後，人皆謂明公棄恩忘本，今日誰肯復以所有之兵束手委公乎！

translations.literal: Since Zhai Rang was executed all say you cast aside gratitude and forgot your origins—who today would willingly hand over troops to you!
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhai Rang was killed, everyone says you cast aside gratitude and forgot where you came from—who today would willingly hand over his troops to you!

sentences.zh: 彼必慮公見奪，逆相拒抗，一朝失勢，豈有容足之地哉！

translations.literal: They will fear you mean to seize their forces and resist you—lose power once and where will you stand!
translations.idiomatic: They will fear you mean to seize their armies and resist you—lose your footing once and where will you have room to stand!

sentences.zh: 自非荷恩殊厚者，詎能深言不諱乎！

translations.literal: Unless one owed you extraordinary grace, who would speak so bluntly!
translations.idiomatic: Unless a man owed you deep gratitude, who would speak so frankly!

sentences.zh: 願明公熟思之，但恐大福不再。

translations.literal: I beg you weigh this carefully—I fear great fortune will not come twice.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you think this through—I fear great fortune will not come twice.

sentences.zh: 苟明公有所措身，閏甫亦何辭就戮！」

translations.literal: If you find a place to stand, Runfu has no complaint about being executed!"
translations.idiomatic: If you find a place to stand, Runfu will have no complaint about dying!"

sentences.zh: 密大怒，揮刃欲擊之；

translations.literal: Mi was furious and swung his blade to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi flew into a rage and raised his blade to strike him.

sentences.zh: 王伯當等固請，乃釋之。

translations.literal: Wang Bodang and others urgently pleaded and he released him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bodang and the others pleaded hard, and he let him go.

sentences.zh: 閏甫奔熊州。

translations.literal: Runfu fled to Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Runfu fled to Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯當亦止密，以為未可，密不從。

translations.literal: Bodang also urged Mi to stop, holding it premature; Mi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Bodang also tried to stop Mi, saying the time was not right, but Mi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 伯當乃曰：「義士之志，不以存亡易心。

translations.literal: Bodang then said, "A man of honor does not change his heart for life or death.
translations.idiomatic: Bodang then said, "A loyal man's resolve does not change with life or death.

sentences.zh: 公必不聽，伯當與公同死耳，然終恐無益也。」

translations.literal: If you will not listen, Bodang dies with you—yet I fear in the end it will help nothing."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not listen, Bodang will die with you—but I fear in the end it will do no good."

sentences.zh: 密因執使者，斬之。

translations.literal: Mi then seized the envoy and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi then seized the envoy and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 庚子旦，密紿桃林縣官曰：「奉詔暫還京師，家人請寄縣捨。」

translations.literal: At dawn on gengzi Mi deceived the officials of Taolin County, saying, "By imperial order I am returning temporarily to the capital; my household asks to lodge at the county quarters."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on gengzi Mi deceived the officials of Taolin County, saying, "By imperial order I am returning briefly to the capital; my family asks to lodge at the county quarters."

sentences.zh: 乃簡驍勇數十人，著婦人衣，戴羃□，藏刀裙下，詐為妻妾，自帥之入縣捨。

translations.literal: He then selected several dozen fierce warriors, dressed them in women's clothes, veiled hoods on their heads, swords hidden beneath their skirts, posing as wives and concubines; he led them personally into the county quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He then picked several dozen fierce fighters, dressed them in women's clothes with veiled hoods, hid swords beneath their skirts, and passed them off as wives and concubines; he led them personally into the county quarters.

sentences.zh: 須臾，變服突出，因據縣城。

translations.literal: In a moment they changed clothes and burst out, seizing the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: In moments they changed clothes, burst out, and seized the county seat.

sentences.zh: 驅掠徒眾，直趣南山，乘險而東，遣人馳告故將伊州刺史襄城張善相，令以兵應接。

translations.literal: Driving and plundering conscript levies, he headed straight for the Southern Mountains, using the difficult terrain to go east, and sent a rider in haste to notify his former general Zhang Shanxiang of Yizhou in Xiangcheng to bring troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Driving conscripts before him and plundering as he went, he headed straight for the Southern Mountains, used the rugged terrain to turn east, and sent a fast rider to his former general Zhang Shanxiang, governor of Yizhou in Xiangcheng, to bring troops and meet him.

sentences.zh: 右翊衛將軍史萬寶鎮熊州，謂行軍總管盛彥師曰：「李密，驍賊也，又輔以王伯當，今決策而叛，殆不可當也。」

translations.literal: Right Upright Guard General Shi Wanbao was stationed at Xiong Prefecture; he said to campaign commander Sheng Yanshi, "Li Mi is a fierce bandit, aided moreover by Wang Bodang; now that he has resolved on rebellion he is nearly impossible to check."
translations.idiomatic: Right Upright Guard General Shi Wanbao was stationed at Xiong Prefecture. He told campaign commander Sheng Yanshi, "Li Mi is a fierce rebel, and with Wang Bodang at his side he has now chosen open revolt—he will be hard to stop."

sentences.zh: 彥師笑曰：「請以數千之眾邀之，必梟其首。」

translations.literal: Yanshi laughed and said, "Give me a few thousand men to intercept him and I will certainly take his head."
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi laughed. "Give me a few thousand men to intercept him and I will take his head for certain."

sentences.zh: 萬寶曰：「公以何策能爾？」

translations.literal: Wanbao said, "By what stratagem can you do that?"
translations.idiomatic: Wanbao asked, "What plan could make that possible?"

sentences.zh: 彥師曰：「兵法尚詐，不可為公言之。」

translations.literal: Yanshi said, "The art of war prizes deception—I cannot tell you."
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi said, "The art of war favors deception—I cannot tell you."

sentences.zh: 即帥眾逾熊耳山南，據要道，令弓弩夾路乘高，刀楯伏於溪谷，令之曰：「俟賊半渡，一時俱發。」

translations.literal: He immediately led troops over the southern face of Mount Xiong'er, held the vital road, ordered crossbowmen lining the heights on both sides of the road, sword-and-shield men hidden in ravines and gullies, and commanded them, "Wait until the rebels are half across, then launch together."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately led his troops over the southern slope of Mount Xiong'er, seized the vital road, posted crossbowmen on the heights along both sides of the path, and hid sword-and-shield men in the ravines, ordering them, "Wait until the rebels are half across, then strike all at once."

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「聞李密欲向洛州，而公入山，何也？」

translations.literal: Someone asked, "We hear Li Mi intends to march on Luo Prefecture—why do you enter the mountains?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "We hear Li Mi means to march on Luo Prefecture—why are you going into the mountains?"

sentences.zh: 彥師曰：「密聲言向洛，實欲出人不意，走襄城，就張善相耳。

translations.literal: Yanshi said, "Mi claims he is heading for Luo but truly means to catch men off guard, flee to Xiangcheng, and join Zhang Shanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi said, "Mi says he is heading for Luo, but he truly means to catch us off guard, flee to Xiangcheng, and join Zhang Shanxiang.

sentences.zh: 若賊入谷口，我自後追之，山路險隘，無所施力，一夫殿後，必不能制。

translations.literal: If the rebels entered the valley mouth and I pursued from behind, the road is narrow and steep with nowhere to deploy force—a single man holding the rear could not be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels entered the valley and I pursued from behind, the road is narrow and steep and there is no room to deploy force—one man holding the rear could hold us off.

sentences.zh: 今吾先得入谷，擒之必矣。」

translations.literal: Now that I enter the valley first, capture is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I enter the valley first, capture is certain."

sentences.zh: 李密既渡陝，以為餘不足慮，遂擁眾徐行，果逾山南出。

translations.literal: After Li Mi had crossed into Shan Prefecture he thought nothing else need worry him; he therefore led his followers at an easy pace and indeed crossed south of the mountains to emerge.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi had crossed into Shan Prefecture he thought he had little left to fear, so he led his men at an easy pace and indeed crossed south of the mountains to emerge.

sentences.zh: 彥師擊之，密眾首尾斷絕，不得相救。

translations.literal: Yanshi struck him; Mi's host was cut head from tail and could not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi attacked him; Mi's force was cut in two and could not rescue itself.

sentences.zh: 遂斬密及伯當，俱傳首長安。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Mi and Bodang and sent both heads to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then beheaded Mi and Bodang and sent both heads to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 彥師以功賜爵葛國公，仍領熊州。

translations.literal: Yanshi for his merit was granted the title Duke of Ge and continued to command Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Yanshi was enfeoffed as Duke of Ge and continued to command Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李世勣在黎陽，上遣使以密首示之，告以反狀。

translations.literal: Li Shiji was at Liyang; Emperor Gaozu sent an envoy to show him Mi's head and report the details of the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji was at Liyang. Emperor Gaozu sent an envoy to show him Li Mi's head and report how he had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 世勣北面拜伏號慟，表請收葬；

translations.literal: Shiji faced north, bowed prostrate and wailed; he submitted a memorial requesting burial.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji turned north, bowed to the ground, and wailed aloud; he submitted a memorial asking to bury the body.

sentences.zh: 詔歸其屍。

translations.literal: An edict returned the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the body returned.

sentences.zh: 世勣為之行服，備君臣之禮。

translations.literal: Shiji wore mourning garb for him and performed the full rites between lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji wore mourning for him and performed the full rites due between lord and minister.

sentences.zh: 大具儀衛，舉軍縞素，葬密於黎陽山南。

translations.literal: With full ceremonial escort, the entire army in white mourning, he buried Mi south of the mountains at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: With full ceremonial escort and the whole army in white mourning, he buried Li Mi south of the mountains at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 密素得士心，哭者多歐血。

translations.literal: Mi had always won men's hearts; many who wept vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi had always won men's hearts; many mourners wept until they spat blood.

sentences.zh: 隋右武衛大將軍李景守北平，高開道圍之，歲余不能克。

translations.literal: Sui Right Martial Guard General Li Jing held Beiping; Gao Kaidao besieged him for more than a year without taking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Right Martial Guard General Li Jing held Beiping; Gao Kaidao besieged him for more than a year without success.

sentences.zh: 遼西太守鄧暠將兵救之，景帥其眾遷於柳城；

translations.literal: Liaoxi Administrator Deng Hao led troops to relieve him; Jing led his followers to relocate to Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi Administrator Deng Hao led troops to relieve him; Jing moved his followers to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 後將還幽州，於道為盜所殺。

translations.literal: Later when about to return to You Prefecture he was killed by bandits on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as he was returning to You Prefecture, bandits killed him on the road.

sentences.zh: 開道遂取北平，進陷漁陽郡，有馬數千匹，眾且萬，自稱燕王，改元始興，都漁陽。

translations.literal: Kaidao then took Beiping, advanced and seized Yuyang Commandery, had several thousand horses, followers nearing ten thousand, styled himself King of Yan, changed the era to Shixing, and made Yuyang his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao then took Beiping, advanced to seize Yuyang Commandery, gathered several thousand horses and nearly ten thousand followers, styled himself King of Yan, adopted the era Shixing, and made Yuyang his capital.

sentences.zh: 懷戎沙門高曇晟因縣令設齋，士民大集，曇晟與僧五千人擁齋眾而反，殺縣令及鎮將，自稱大乘皇帝，立尼靜宣為邪輸皇后，改元法輪。

translations.literal: At Huairong the monk Gao Tansheng, when the magistrate held a vegetarian feast and officials and people gathered in great numbers, with five thousand monks seized the feast crowd and rebelled, killed the magistrate and garrison commander, styled himself Emperor of Great Vehicle, installed the nun Jing Xuan as Empress of Evil Wheel, and changed the era to Falun.
translations.idiomatic: At Huairong the monk Gao Tansheng, when the magistrate held a vegetarian feast and a great crowd of officials and commoners gathered, rebelled with five thousand monks, seized the assembly, killed the magistrate and garrison commander, styled himself Emperor of the Great Vehicle, installed the nun Jing Xuan as Empress of Evil Wheel, and adopted the era Falun.

sentences.zh: 遣使招開道，立為齊王。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to summon Kaidao and enfeoffed him as King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to summon Gao Kaidao and enfeoffed him as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 開道帥眾五千人歸之，居數月，襲殺曇晟，悉並其眾。

translations.literal: Kaidao led five thousand men to join him; after several months he attacked and killed Tansheng and absorbed all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao led five thousand men to join him; after several months he attacked and killed Tansheng and absorbed all his followers.

sentences.zh: 有犯法不至死者，上特命殺之。

translations.literal: Someone had violated the law but did not deserve death; Emperor Gaozu specially ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had broken the law but did not deserve death; Emperor Gaozu specially ordered him put to death.

sentences.zh: 監察御史李素立諫曰：「三尺法，王者所與天下共也；

translations.literal: Censor Li Suli remonstrated, saying, "The law measured by the three-foot rod is what the king shares with all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Suli remonstrated, saying, "The law measured by the three-foot rod is what a ruler shares with all under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 法一動搖，人無所措手足。

translations.literal: Once the law trembles, people have nowhere to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: Once the law wavers, people do not know where to put hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 陛下甫創鴻業，奈何棄法！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has just begun the great enterprise—how can you abandon the law!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has just begun the great enterprise—how can you cast the law aside!

sentences.zh: 臣忝法司，不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: I, who shamefully hold office in the law, dare not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: I hold office in the law and dare not obey such an edict."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 自是特承恩遇，命所司授以七品清要官；

translations.literal: From then on Suli received special favor; the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to grant him a seventh-rank position both important and pure.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Suli received special favor; the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to grant him a seventh-rank post both important and pure.

sentences.zh: 所司擬雍州司戶，上曰：「此官要而不清。」

translations.literal: The offices proposed him as Registrar of Yong Prefecture; Emperor Gaozu said, "That office is important but not pure."
translations.idiomatic: The offices proposed him as registrar of Yong Prefecture; Emperor Gaozu said, "That post is important but not pure."

sentences.zh: 又擬秘書郎。

translations.literal: They then proposed Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: They then proposed secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此官清而不要。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "That office is pure but not important."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "That post is pure but not important."

sentences.zh: 遂擢授侍御史。

translations.literal: He was therefore promoted and appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore promoted and appointed attending censor.

sentences.zh: 素立，義深之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Suli was the great-grandson of Li Yishen.
translations.idiomatic: Suli was the great-grandson of Li Yishen.

sentences.zh: 上以舞胡安叱奴為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed the dancing Hu An Chinu as Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu appointed the Hu dancer An Chinu as attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李綱諫曰：「古者樂工不與士齒，雖賢如子野、師襄，皆終身繼世不易其業。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Li Gang remonstrated, saying, "In antiquity music workers did not rank with scholars; though as talented as Zhi Ye and Shi Xiang, they spent their lives in hereditary craft and never changed their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Gang remonstrated, saying, "In antiquity musicians did not rank with scholars; though as gifted as Zhi Ye and Shi Xiang, they spent their lives in hereditary craft and never changed their trade.

sentences.zh: 唯齊末封曹妙達為王，安馬駒為開府，有國家者以為殷鑒。

translations.literal: Only at the end of Qi were Cao Miaoda made a king and An Maju made an honorary commander—statesmen took that as a dire warning.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the end of Qi were Cao Miaoda made a king and An Maju made an honorary commander—rulers took that as a warning.

sentences.zh: 今天下新定，建義功臣，行賞未遍，高才碩學，猶滯草萊；

translations.literal: Today the realm is newly settled—meritorious founders have not all been rewarded, men of great talent and learning still languish in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is newly settled—founding merit has not all been rewarded, and men of great talent and learning still languish in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 而先擢舞胡為五品，使鳴玉曳組，趨翔廊廟，非所以規模後世也。」

translations.literal: Yet you promote a dancing Hu to fifth rank, let him jangle jade pendants at court—this is no model for posterity."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you promote a Hu dancer to fifth rank, let him jangle jade pendants and stride through the halls of state—this is no model for posterity."

sentences.zh: 上不從，曰：「吾業已授之，不可追也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu would not listen and said, "I have already granted it—it cannot be withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu would not listen and said, "I have already granted it—it cannot be taken back.

sentences.zh: 陳岳論曰：受命之主，發號施令，為子孫法；

translations.literal: Chen Yue remarked: A ruler who receives the Mandate issues orders and commands as law for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue remarked: A ruler who receives the Mandate issues orders and commands that become law for posterity.

sentences.zh: 一不中理，則為厲階。

translations.literal: One that misses reason becomes a path of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: One misstep becomes a path to disaster.

sentences.zh: 今高祖曰：「業已授之，不可追」，苟授之而是，則已；

translations.literal: Now Emperor Gaozu said, "Already granted—it cannot be withdrawn"; if the grant were right, well enough.
translations.idiomatic: Now Emperor Gaozu said, "Already granted—it cannot be taken back"; if the grant were right, that would be one thing.

sentences.zh: 授之而非，胡不可追歟！

translations.literal: If the grant was wrong, why can it not be taken back!
translations.idiomatic: If the appointment was a mistake, why not take it back!

sentences.zh: 君人之道，不得不以「業已授之」為誡哉！

translations.literal: In the way of ruling men, must one not take "it has already been granted" as a warning!
translations.idiomatic: Surely a ruler must not treat "already granted" as an excuse never to correct a mistake!

sentences.zh: 李軌吏部尚書梁碩，有智略，軌常倚之以為謀主。

translations.literal: Liang Shuo, Minister of Personnel under Li Gui, was resourceful and strategic; Gui often relied on him as his chief planner.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo, Li Gui's Minister of Personnel, was clever and far-sighted; Gui relied on him as his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 碩見諸胡浸盛，陰勸軌宜加防察，由是與戶部尚書安修仁有隙。

translations.literal: Shuo saw the various Hu growing ever stronger and secretly urged Gui to strengthen precautions; thereby he fell out with An Xiuren, Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo saw the Hu growing stronger and quietly urged Gui to guard against them; he thus quarreled with Minister of Revenue An Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 軌子仲琰嘗詣碩，碩不為禮，乃與修仁共譖碩於軌，誣以謀反，軌鴆碩，殺之。

translations.literal: Gui's son Zhongyan once visited Shuo, and Shuo did not treat him with courtesy; Zhongyan then joined Xiuren in slandering Shuo to Gui, falsely charging him with plotting rebellion; Gui poisoned Shuo and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's son Zhongyan once called on Shuo, who slighted him; Zhongyan and Xiuren then slandered Shuo to Gui as a traitor; Gui poisoned him and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 有胡巫謂軌曰：「上帝當遣玉女自天而降。」

translations.literal: A Hu shaman told Gui, "Heaven will send a jade maiden down from the sky."
translations.idiomatic: A Hu shaman told Gui, "Heaven will send a jade maiden down from the sky."

sentences.zh: 軌信之，發民築台以候玉女，勞費甚廣。

translations.literal: Gui believed it, mobilized the people to build a terrace to await the jade maiden, and spent vast labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Gui believed him, conscripted labor to build a terrace for the maiden, and wasted enormous resources.

sentences.zh: 河右饑，人相食，軌傾家財以賑之；

translations.literal: Famine struck west of the Yellow River and men ate one another; Gui poured out his family wealth to relieve them;
translations.idiomatic: West of the Yellow River famine drove men to cannibalism; Gui spent his family fortune on relief;

sentences.zh: 不足，欲發倉粟，召群臣議之。

translations.literal: it was not enough, and he wished to open the granary grain; he summoned the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: when that was not enough he wanted to open the state granaries and called his ministers to debate it.

sentences.zh: 曹珍等皆曰：「國以民為本，豈可愛倉粟而坐視其死乎！」

translations.literal: Cao Zhen and others all said, "A state takes the people as its foundation — how can we cherish granary grain and sit watching them die!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen and others said, "A state rests on its people — how can we hoard grain and watch them starve!"

sentences.zh: 謝統師等皆故隋官，心終不服，密與群胡為黨，排軌故人，乃詬珍曰：「百姓餓者自是羸弱，勇壯之士終不至此。

translations.literal: Xie Tongshi and others were all former Sui officials who in their hearts never submitted; they secretly allied with the Hu cliques, pushed aside Gui's old companions, and reviled Zhen, saying, "Those among the common people who starve are naturally the weak; stout and brave men will never come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tongshi and other former Sui officials, never loyal at heart, secretly sided with the Hu, sidelined Gui's old followers, and attacked Zhen: "Only the weak starve; strong men never sink so low.

sentences.zh: 國家倉粟以備不虞，豈可散之以飼羸弱！

translations.literal: The state's granary grain is kept against the unexpected — how can we scatter it to feed the feeble!
translations.idiomatic: State grain is for emergencies — we cannot scatter it on the weak!

sentences.zh: 僕射苟悅人情，不為國計，非忠臣也。」

translations.literal: The Vice Director curries favor with the crowd and does not plan for the state — he is no loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director panders to the mob instead of serving the state — he is no loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 軌以為然，由是士民離怨。

translations.literal: Gui thought this correct, and from this scholars and commoners turned away in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed, and gentry and people alike turned against him in anger.
